quick.expression.placeholder.meaning: Invites the user to enter a mathematical expression.
quick.expression.placeholder.context: Shown only while the quick input is empty.
quick.expression.placeholder.location: Inside the centered quick calculation input.

quick.expression.accessibleName.meaning: Names the mathematical input for assistive technology.
quick.expression.accessibleName.context: Read when the quick input receives focus, including when a value is present.
quick.expression.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the quick input; not an extra visible label.

quick.result.label.meaning: Identifies the value produced by the current expression.
quick.result.label.context: Used only when a valid result for the current expression is available. The result line is empty for unfinished input, and an earlier result must not stand in for the current one. Decimal formatting and reduced opacity of trailing digits are handled separately from this label.
quick.result.label.location: Result line directly below the quick input.

result.boolean.true.meaning: Displays a logical result whose value is true.
result.boolean.true.context: Used when the current valid calculation produces a logical value, such as 5 > 3. This is display text; accepted input literals remain separate. Quick result copy preserves the displayed localized text. Round 23 accepts separate input symbols true/false plus да/нет when ru is active; see values/catalog.json. Display and copy remain these localized Yes/No texts. if/and/or/not require logical operands, without numeric coercion; arithmetic with a logical value is rejected.
result.boolean.true.location: The active calculation result, directly below quick input or in the result area associated with an expression in a calculation sheet.

result.boolean.false.meaning: Displays a logical result whose value is false.
result.boolean.false.context: Used when the current valid calculation produces a logical value, such as 5 < 3. This is a valid result, not an error or a missing result. Accepted input literals remain separate. Quick result copy preserves the displayed localized text. Round 23 accepts separate input symbols true/false plus да/нет when ru is active; see values/catalog.json. Display and copy remain these localized Yes/No texts. if/and/or/not require logical operands, without numeric coercion; arithmetic with a logical value is rejected.
result.boolean.false.location: The active calculation result, directly below quick input or in the result area associated with an expression in a calculation sheet.

completion.list.accessibleName.meaning: Names the list of suggested expression completions for assistive technology.
completion.list.accessibleName.context: Used when suggestions open from the first letter in quick or multiline input, or immediately after a complete :: or to conversion operator. Up to seven rows are visible; arrow selection scrolls to keep the active option visible. While open, Up and Down select, Tab accepts, and Escape closes only the suggestions. Compatible target units are suggested after a conversion operator; comments do not open suggestions. Search ordering is still being specified.
completion.list.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the suggestion list aligned beneath the currently typed word. One frame surrounds the list, which overlays following text without shifting it and may cross the input area's lower boundary. A visible heading is not required.

completion.showDescription.meaning: Opens the complete description of the selected suggestion when the inline text is shortened.
completion.showDescription.context: F1 opens the full description of the selected suggestion; without a selection it opens general help. Pointer hover also exposes the full text. Escape restores the prior focus. User-authored descriptions remain in their original language; exact geometry is subject to the visual prototype.
completion.showDescription.location: Command or keyboard help associated with the selected suggestion. The exact control placement belongs to the full interface prototype.

completion.function.sin.description.text: Sine. Enter the angle in degrees.
completion.function.sin.description.meaning: Explains that the ordinary sine call takes its unmarked numeric argument in degrees.
completion.function.sin.description.context: Shown when the sine function is suggested. Ordinary input such as sin(30) uses degrees without a suffix; explicitly marked radian input such as sin(pi/2 rad) is also supported. Both behaviors were reconfirmed in expression-language round 15. The typed matching prefix is visually reduced in opacity; the proposed continuation is fully opaque.
completion.function.sin.description.location: Immediately after the complete sine signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. The description uses the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, with no shared-column or right-edge alignment.

completion.function.sqrt.description.text: Square root of a nonnegative number.
completion.function.sqrt.description.meaning: Explains the square root function within the calculator's real-number domain.
completion.function.sqrt.description.context: Description shown when the square root function is suggested. Negative real arguments are outside the accepted numeric domain. The typed matching prefix is visually reduced in opacity; the proposed continuation is fully opaque.
completion.function.sqrt.description.location: Immediately after the complete square-root signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. The description uses the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, with no shared-column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.squareMetre.description.meaning: Identifies a square metre as a unit of area.
completion.unit.squareMetre.description.context: Shown when this area or volume unit is offered as a completion. Tab inserts the displayed superscript unit symbol. Contextual-units round 8 extends shorthand 2/3 formatting to every known length symbol, including explicit length aliases, but only to whole symbols; a longer name prefix must not be rewritten. Backspace deletes the exponent and formatting adds no separate undo step. m2/m3 never denote minutes. A caret raises a whole quantity and is not an equivalent completion spelling. Pasted formula text follows the same formatting and has one undo for the entire paste; selected formula text is copied with visible ²/³ characters. Numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript but preserves displayed numeric rounding in quick mode, history and sheets. See the context-specific copy help for targeting and focus.
completion.unit.squareMetre.description.location: Immediately after the unit spelling in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.cubicMetre.description.context: Shown when this area or volume unit is offered as a completion. Tab inserts the displayed superscript unit symbol. completion.unit.cubicMetre.description.location: Immediately after the unit spelling in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.squareCentimetre.descrip.meaning: Identifies a square centimetre as a unit of area.

completion.unit.squareCentimetre.descrip.location: Immediately after the unit spelling in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without column or right-edge alignment.

completion.unit.cubicCentimetre.descript.meaning: Identifies a cubic centimetre as a unit of volume.
completion.unit.cubicCentimetre.descript.context: Shown when this area or volume unit is offered as a completion. Tab inserts the displayed superscript unit symbol. Contextual-units round 8 extends shorthand 2/3 formatting to every known length symbol, including explicit length aliases, but only to whole symbols; a longer name prefix must not be rewritten. quick.history.show.context: With the completion menu closed, Up Arrow in quick mode expands history and immediately recalls the preceding saved formula into the fixed input; repeated Up presses recall older formulas while the list moves downward through the console. Preserve the original input and cursor/selection from before browsing so Down can return to it. An open completion menu retains its existing arrow-key priority. The proposed separate Tab history mode was not accepted. Expanded-mode opening uses a separate Alt+Up command accepted in copying round 16; see help.history.extendedShortcutRule.
quick.history.show.location: Command menu or keyboard hint associated with quick input.

quick.history.hide.meaning: Collapses history while retaining the quick input.
quick.history.hide.context: Available when history is expanded. Round 17 accepts automatic collapse when Down Arrow returns to the original input, whether empty or nonempty, restoring its cursor/selection. Further Down at the original input does not erase it. Up stops at the oldest saved entry. Successful ordinary Enter confirmation also collapses history. These quick-mode boundaries do not change the separate search or expanded-sheet history contexts.
quick.history.hide.location: Command menu or keyboard hint associated with expanded history.

quick.sheet.open.meaning: Switches to a calculation with variables and multiple expressions.
quick.sheet.open.context: Ctrl+Shift+Enter on Windows or Cmd+Shift+Enter on macOS opens a new sheet with the quick draft on its first line at the same screen position, expanding downward. Returning preserves the sheet and restores the preceding quick draft. Native shortcut registration still requires validation.

quick.hide.meaning: Dismisses the visible calculator without naming a full application exit.
quick.hide.context: Used by Escape when suggestions are closed, the repeated summon shortcut, or a click on another application. If suggestions are open, the first Escape closes only the suggestions. The unfinished input is preserved when the calculator hides.
quick.hide.location: Command menu or keyboard help; not standard window chrome.

definitions.saveConstant.meaning: Publishes a user-defined named formula for reuse, retaining its dependencies on other saved constants.
definitions.saveConstant.context: Explicit publication under round 18. A draft does not change the working definition before Save. Correct publication recalculates current quick input and open dependent sheets; invalid syntax, unknown references or forbidden cycles preserve the working version and the editable draft. Assigning or autosaving a local sheet variable does not publish it globally. New definitions must not silently overwrite an existing global name. The header comment description is published with the definition. Exact action access and storage-failure handling remain separate design work.
definitions.saveConstant.location: Definition actions associated with the calculation editor; the exact menu placement is not yet specified.

definitions.saveFunction.meaning: Saves a user-defined calculation rule for future calls by name.
definitions.saveFunction.context: Explicit publication under round 18 for short or multiline functions with sequential local intermediates and a final result expression. Parameters and own locals resolve alongside saved global definitions, without implicit caller-sheet capture. Invalid syntax, unknown references, recursion or cycles preserve the working version and draft. Validation is not a guarantee of success for every numerical argument. Header descriptions publish with the definition. Current dependent calculations recalculate; saved history answers do not. Exact action access and storage-failure handling remain separate design work.
definitions.saveFunction.location: Definition actions associated with the calculation editor; the exact menu placement is not yet specified.

copy.result.meaning: Copies the targeted valid calculation result.
copy.result.context: Accepted through copying round 2: Ctrl+C on Windows / Cmd+C on macOS in the editor with no text selection copies the single ready displayed result entry, even if that entry groups several interpretations. Click copy targets the clicked entry. Numeric result copy omits the unit: 4m copies 4, and 5m/s copies 5. Preserve displayed numeric rounding, all shown digits, signs, numeral-system prefix/case and grouping; do not copy hidden precision or change working values. Formula selection copies the selected visible text, including units. If multiple displayed entries exist while the editor has focus and no text is selected, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and shows copy.chooseResult. Count all entries after display grouping, including horizontal overflow. Quick copy keeps the window, formula and cursor, restores input focus after a click and creates no history. Missing or stale results of the current input cannot be copied. Round 15 accepts clicking a displayed history answer to copy its saved displayed value without recalculation. Changes to constants or functions do not make that historical answer ineligible; use the saved answer that was clicked, not the currently calculated value or the answer chosen at confirmation. Preserve the current formula and cursor, return focus to input and leave the stored record and confirmation choice unchanged. The same numeric-only and localized logical payload rules apply. Keyboard selection for confirmation was accepted in round 6. Round 14 accepts Ctrl+C/Cmd+C while focus is in the current result row: copy the highlighted ready answer and keep selection and focus there. An inactive text selection retained in the editor does not change this target. The editor copy shortcut retains its accepted behavior. Enter confirmation is a separate accepted action: in quick mode with one ready displayed result, it records history and copies with the same payload rules, then starts empty input while keeping the window open. Enter never accepts a completion suggestion. Round 17 accepts keyboard copy in history opened from an expanded sheet: Up/Down choose a record, Left/Right choose a saved answer and Ctrl+C/Cmd+C copies that answer with the same payload, preserving the sheet and history focus. This is not copying a freshly evaluated sheet expression or recalling its formula; Enter separately inserts the formula. Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers. Round 24 adds calendar answers: copy the complete displayed date/time/day-carry/offset text, not a numeric timestamp or a unitless date component. Selected source text stays literal, saved history stays immutable, and dynamic copy/confirmation uses the coherent ready result set already shown. Round 25 copies the complete displayed calendar period with units and both calendar/fixed parts. When the calendar-month component normalizes to zero, it is an ordinary fixed duration and retains numeric-coefficient-only copy. This does not change physical-quantity copy or the percentage fraction exception. Round 27 accepts approximately zero as a ready result. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. Exact zero and approximate zero are distinct display entries; identical approximate entries group while retaining every latent value. Multiple visible entries still require choosing. Selected source text remains literal.
copy.result.location: Copy command for a ready current result in quick mode or a sheet, or for a selected saved history answer. The active surface determines the target.

copy.success.meaning: Confirms that the clipboard write succeeded.
copy.success.context: Feedback only after a result has actually been written to the clipboard successfully. Ctrl+C/Cmd+C and click quick copy preserve input and add no history. Full quick-mode confirmation success also requires saving history: Enter then starts empty input in the open window, while Ctrl+Enter on Windows / Cmd+Enter on macOS hides the window with empty input on the next invocation. This message confirms only the clipboard write and must not imply that a failed history write succeeded or that selected formula text was copied as a result. A confirmation failure preserves the formula, result and open window. Successful Enter also collapses expanded history; failure does not. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula, calculation or chosen answer must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Exact feedback presentation remains open. For quick copy with focus in the current result row, keep focus and selection on the highlighted answer; this feedback must not move focus back to the editor. Clicking a current answer still returns focus to input. Round 15 accepts click-copy of a saved historical answer, preserving the current formula and cursor and returning focus to input. Report success for the saved displayed value actually copied, without recalculating it or changing history. For accepted round-17 clipboard copy in expanded-sheet history, the success feedback must preserve history focus and the unchanged sheet; it does not imply formula insertion or a new history record.
copy.success.location: Brief copy feedback associated with the input/result region and its accessible live region. Presentation when confirmation resets input or hides the window is to be verified.

copy.error.text: Could not copy the result. Try again.
copy.error.meaning: Reports that writing the result to the clipboard failed.
copy.error.context: Shown or announced only when writing a result to the clipboard fails, including shortcut/click quick copy and the copy step of Enter or modified-Enter confirmation. A failed quick-mode confirmation preserves the formula, result and open window and shows this brief error; it must not clear input or hide the window. Do not use this message for a history-save failure or claim success. Retrying an incomplete confirmation without changing the formula, calculation or chosen answer must not duplicate an already saved history entry; after full success, apply the command used for the retry. Operation order and recovery after restart remain architecture decisions. Failed confirmation also preserves the expanded history state. Copying a formula selection is a separate operation. Result-row shortcut copy uses the highlighted current answer; it does not fall back to copying an inactive editor selection. Quick copy does not confirm a calculation. This feedback also covers clipboard failure after clicking a saved history answer. Do not recalculate the historical expression or substitute a current answer as a fallback; do not claim a successful copy.
copy.error.location: Feedback area near the active result.

expression.invalid.meaning: Reports an expression that cannot be parsed.
expression.invalid.context: Shown for a syntax error after the agreed validation trigger.
expression.invalid.location: Diagnostic area associated with the current expression.

expression.divisionByZero.meaning: Explains why division cannot produce a result.
expression.divisionByZero.context: Shown when the current expression attempts division by zero during evaluation. The expression has no copyable result. An unselected conditional branch is not evaluated and must not trigger this message.
expression.divisionByZero.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.unknownName.meaning: Reports an identifier that the calculation cannot resolve.
expression.unknownName.context: Shown when an expression refers to an undefined name.
expression.unknownName.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

placeholders.name: An identifier exactly as written by the user in the calculation. Preserve its spelling and do not translate the inserted value.

expression.domainError.text: This operation is not defined for these values
expression.domainError.meaning: Reports values outside the supported mathematical domain.
expression.domainError.context: Shown when a supported operation cannot accept the supplied values.
expression.domainError.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.incompatibleUnits.meaning: Reports a conversion between incompatible measurement dimensions.
expression.incompatibleUnits.context: Shown when the requested unit conversion is invalid.
expression.incompatibleUnits.location: Diagnostic area associated with the conversion expression.

expression.unknownUnit.meaning: Reports a measurement unit that the calculator does not recognize.
expression.unknownUnit.context: Shown when a conversion uses an unsupported unit token.
expression.unknownUnit.location: Diagnostic area associated with the conversion expression.

placeholders.unit: A unit token exactly as written in the expression. Preserve the token; accepted unit spellings are defined by the expression language.

expression.precisionLimit.meaning: Explains that an entered number exceeds the supported numeric precision.
expression.precisionLimit.context: Shown for decimal input exceeding the supported 30-significant-digit precision. The input must not be silently truncated. Integer magnitude is checked independently of the number of written digits in the selected base and uses the dedicated integer-limit diagnostic. Exact rounding at the working-precision boundary remains under discussion. Round 26 distinguishes entered literals exceeding 30 significant digits, which are rejected, from computed fractional results, which are rounded to 30 significant digits with exact ties away from zero. Do not use this input diagnostic merely because an operation has an infinite decimal expansion.
expression.precisionLimit.location: Diagnostic area for the affected expression or sheet line.

expression.limit.text: This calculation exceeds the supported limits
expression.limit.meaning: Explains that evaluation stopped at a configured computational limit.
expression.limit.context: Shown when an expression is rejected for exceeding the supported complexity or evaluation budget. Long-running calculation mode is excluded; exact resource thresholds remain to be specified.
expression.limit.location: Diagnostic area for the affected calculation.

history.title.meaning: Names the list of past calculations.
history.title.context: Shown when the history view is expanded. Successful Enter confirmation in quick mode with one ready displayed result adds the calculation to history, copies its result, starts empty input and collapses expanded history. Arrow Up opens it again with the newest calculation nearest to the stationary input. Failed confirmation does not collapse history. The history expansion state on the next invocation after modified-Enter hiding is not yet selected. Copying round 7 fixes historical results at confirmation; changed constants or functions do not recalculate them. Recalling a formula into input calculates a new result with current definitions while preserving the original record.
history.title.location: Heading of the history region above the stationary quick input. Initially the newest entry is closest to the input; Arrow Up shifts the list downward into the console and Arrow Down shifts it upward.

history.empty.context: Shown when history contains no saved entries.

history.search.placeholder.meaning: Invites a search among past calculations.
history.search.placeholder.context: Search was accepted in copying round 9. Ctrl+F on Windows / Cmd+F on macOS in active quick mode opens history search over saved formulas and results. Preserve the current formula and its cursor and do not move its input field. Searching must not recalculate historical records. Copying round 10 accepts filtering as the query is typed. Up/Down choose a matching record without replacing the formula. Enter closes search and recalls the chosen formula for recalculation only, without copying, confirmation or new history. Escape restores the original formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. Exact field placement remains open.
history.search.placeholder.location: Search input inside the history region.

history.search.accessibleName.context: Read when the history search input receives focus. The accepted quick-mode search targets saved formulas and historical results, not the live recalculation. Search focus must preserve the formula draft and cursor for later return. Copying round 10 accepts filtering as the query is typed. Up/Down choose a matching record without replacing the formula. Enter closes search and recalls the chosen formula for recalculation only, without copying, confirmation or new history. Escape restores the original formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. Exact field placement remains open.
history.search.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the history search input.

history.noMatches.meaning: Explains why a nonempty history search displays no entries.
history.noMatches.context: Shown when a nonempty search query has no matching saved formula or displayed result. Matching is case-insensitive substring search, updated as the query is typed; Enter recalls nothing without a match. Empty query shows all history in normal order; history.empty describes the state with no saved records. Search does not recalculate records or search only currently loaded rows. Copying round 12 accepts decimal point/comma and numeric digit-grouping equivalents, plus plain/superscript 2/3 in recognized length-unit area/volume spellings in the Latin baseline and active locale. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. See help.history.searchNotationRule. A record may still match its saved displayed result independently of its formula spelling.

history.entry.accessibleName.meaning: Proposes announcing a historical formula and its complete displayed set of saved results.
history.entry.accessibleName.context: Editorial accessible-name draft for a focused history entry. Copying rounds 7 and 8 accept storing the complete result set and showing the formula with all saved displayed answers in one horizontal row. The answer chosen at confirmation is bold when several answers exist; use the separate history.result.chosen description to make that distinction available without relying on font weight alone. Do not add visible interpretation captions, drop saved displayed alternatives or substitute the live recalculation. Exact list announcement and native accessibility behavior require prototype verification.
history.entry.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of a calculation history entry.

placeholders.expression: The historical mathematical formula, formatted for the active locale according to the existing unit-language rules. Do not translate or alter inserted user names or comments.
placeholders.results: The complete formatted set of saved displayed results for this history entry, including unit and numeral-system notation. Do not use the live recalculation or only the copied numeric value. List formatting and selection announcement are handled by the accessibility presentation and remain to be verified.

history.reuse.meaning: Returns the targeted historical formula to input for recalculation.
history.reuse.context: Used for a selected history entry. Accepted in copying round 7: the recalled formula is calculated anew with current user constants and functions; the original history record and its saved results remain unchanged. Navigation that recalls the formula does not itself confirm or create a new record. Successful confirmation records the new calculation under the existing Enter or modified-Enter flow. Retrying an incomplete confirmation with unchanged formula and calculation does not duplicate an already saved entry; copying round 8 accepts a separate record for every new successful confirmation, even when formula and results match an earlier record. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. A specific history entry is required; without one the action is unavailable. Invoking it recalls a copy for recalculation rather than confirming or copying its result.
history.reuse.location: Item in the shared history menu opened by right-clicking a history record or the quick-mode history-menu shortcut.

history.delete.context: Accepted in copying round 9: an explicit history action deletes one particular record without a confirmation dialog and provides history.undo. Identical records from separate confirmations are distinct targets. Constants, functions, sheets and templates are preserved. This does not bind Delete in the formula editor to record deletion. Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Hiding and reopening the window preserve Undo. Restore full removed records in their former order without removing calculations added later. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. It requires a specific target entry and is unavailable without one. Opening the menu is not invocation of deletion. Failure behavior and exact disabled presentation remain open.
history.delete.location: Item in the shared history menu, targeting one specific history record.

history.clear.context: Accepted in copying round 9: starts a separate confirmation before clearing the complete calculation history. Opening this action is not consent to deletion. Constants, functions, sheets and templates are preserved. Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Hiding and reopening the window preserve Undo. Restore full removed records in their former order without removing calculations added later. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Copying round 13 includes this action in the shared history menu; a selected individual history entry is not required. Opening the menu does not start clearing.

history.clear.title.meaning: Asks the user to confirm clearing the calculation history.
history.clear.title.context: Confirmation flow accepted in copying round 9; exact wording is editorial. Shown before clearing the complete calculation history, never for deleting one record. Copying round 10 accepts undoing a full clear as one operation until the application fully exits; hiding the window does not end Undo availability.
history.clear.title.location: Title of the history clearing dialog.

sheet.title.meaning: Names a multi-expression calculation with variables.
sheet.title.context: Used as the generic extended-mode heading.
sheet.title.location: Heading of the extended calculation view.

sheet.name.label.meaning: Labels the user-defined name of a calculation sheet.
sheet.name.label.context: Shown when creating or renaming a saved sheet.
sheet.name.label.location: Label next to the sheet name field.

sheet.name.placeholder.meaning: Invites a name for a calculation sheet.
sheet.name.placeholder.context: Shown while a sheet name field is empty.

sheet.editor.accessibleName.meaning: Names the editor for variables and expressions.
sheet.editor.accessibleName.context: Read when the extended editor receives focus.
sheet.editor.accessibleName.location: Accessible name of the sheet editor.

sheet.new.context: Accepted in round 19: create a separate locally autosaved sheet through the shared library. Closing another sheet does not delete it; this command does not publish global definition drafts. Exact navigation focus and unsaved-storage-error behavior still need design.
sheet.new.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.save.meaning: Saves the current sheet as a reusable local calculation.
sheet.save.context: Unassigned candidate label. Named sheets now autosave under round 17, point 6; the accepted flow does not require a manual Save sheet button. Do not treat this catalog entry as approval of an extra control or as permission to autosave global definitions.

sheet.rename.meaning: Changes the saved name of a sheet.
sheet.rename.context: Available for a named calculation sheet.
sheet.rename.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

sheet.duplicate.meaning: Creates a separate copy of a calculation sheet.
sheet.duplicate.context: Accepted in round 19: creates a sheet with its own text, without modifying the source. Global definition references retain their existing live meaning.
sheet.duplicate.location: Actions for the relevant sheet or template in the shared library or its opened document; exact menu placement remains interface work.

help.precedence.unitPowersRule.text: A final 2 or 3 on a complete known length-unit symbol automatically displays as a superscript: cm2 becomes cm², мм3 becomes мм³, ft2 becomes ft² and metre2 becomes metre². The same rule applies to explicit length aliases and to the Latin baseline plus one active locale. m2/m3 and м2/м3 always mean square/cubic metres, never minutes. Do not format a prefix of a longer name: m20 and m2rate remain unchanged; continuing the word removes the superscript formatting. Backspace immediately after m² deletes only the exponent, leaving m. Undo restores the preceding user input without an extra step for automatic formatting. Pasted formula text receives the same formatting as typed text: 2cm2 + 3cm2 displays as 2cm² + 3cm². One undo restores the state before the entire paste. Copying selected formula text puts the visible text on the clipboard, including actual ²/³ characters. Quick numeric result copy omits the unit and its superscript: 4m² copies 4. Displayed numeric rounding is preserved and the working value is unchanged. The caret ^ raises the entire quantity to a power: 2m2 denotes two square metres; 2m^2 leaves the supported answer 4m², discarding the squared-minutes interpretation. Unit support is checked after final cancellation. Shorthand autoformatting is not extended to time, mass or other dimensions.

Round 9 approves identical formatting for pasted formula text, one undo for the entire paste and visible superscript characters when copying selected formula text. Backspace deletes the exponent and formatting adds no separate undo step. The metre/minute ambiguity is absent from square/cube unit shorthand. Copying round 2 omits units and their superscripts from quick numeric result copy while preserving displayed numeric formatting and working precision. Selected formula text still includes units and superscripts. Other copy commands, editing boundaries, stored-name conflicts and branch-error policies remain open.

help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule.text: Lowercase m can mean a metre or a minute; the active Russian spelling м follows the same rule. Lazy resolution uses the whole formula, including outer parentheses. If multiple interpretations remain valid, show all distinct visible answers: 10m / 2s gives 5m/s or the unitless 300. Identical-looking answers appear once: 2m * 2 displays one 4m. Answers have no interpretation captions and remain in one row with horizontal scrolling when needed. Grouping the display does not discard original meanings or exact values. Explicit metre and min select a unit directly; the Russian equivalents are метр and мин. For m and its local alias, metre interpretations precede minute interpretations.
help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule.meaning: Explains that a visible calculated result may retain an unresolved unit symbol instead of forcing a choice.
help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule.context: Accepted contextual-units round 3 presentation: group identical-looking formatted answers, omit result captions and use horizontal overflow only. Preserve underlying interpretations and exact values. Copying round 16 fixes the known metre/minute interpretation order; see help.results.orderRule. Copying and confirmation are described in their separate accepted interaction-help fragments. Highlighting the first displayed answer is navigation focus, not automatic confirmation or selection of a hidden meaning.
help.precedence.lazyUnitsRule.location: Unit interpretation section in the in-app operator help and its generated documentation previews.

help.precedence.durationNotation.text: Short duration symbols are w, d, h, m, s and ms. Russian symbols are н, д, ч, м, с and мс. Days remain 24 hours and weeks remain seven days. Adjacent duration components add, with or without spaces: 1h30m and 1h 30m both equal 90 minutes. Components may appear in any order and repeat: 30m1h equals 90 minutes; 1h30m15m equals 105 minutes. Use an explicit * to multiply adjacent duration quantities. With only ambiguous m symbols, retain both valid readings: 1m30m and 1m 30m give 31 minutes as a duration sum and 30 square metres as a length product. This does not introduce addition of adjacent lengths. A compound duration is one value for surrounding operators: 1h30m * 2 equals 180 minutes, and -1h30m equals minus 90 minutes. An incomplete final component such as 1h30 keeps the result blank until its unit is entered. An explicit operator is required before a following quantity of a clearly different dimension: 1h30m2km reports a missing operator; write 1h30m / 2km to calculate pace. This boundary does not remove the two accepted readings of 1m30m or other accepted forms of implicit multiplication.
help.precedence.durationNotation.meaning: Explains duration sums, accepted ambiguous readings, treatment as one value under surrounding operators, incomplete input and the boundary before another dimension.
help.precedence.durationNotation.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 7. Keep both operation readings and their values until whole-expression constraints are applied; do not force an ambiguous sequence to mean only duration. Examples describe value and dimension, not a new result notation or result caption. Original input is not automatically reordered. The explicit multiplication requirement applies to adjacent duration quantities, not to a duration followed by a parenthesized scalar expression. An unfinished 1h30 must not retain a stale answer or become multiplication by 30. A following quantity of a clearly different dimension requires an explicit operator. These duration rules do not regroup the separate length-product interpretation. Other token boundaries remain open.
help.precedence.durationNotation.location: Unit interpretation section in the in-app operator help and its generated documentation previews.

result.alternatives.label.meaning: Names the collection of valid answers for different interpretations of one expression.
result.alternatives.label.context: Accessible label for the complete horizontal result row after display grouping. Identical full formatted answers, including units, appear once; interpretation captions remain excluded. Horizontal overflow does not reduce the entry count for copy eligibility. While the formula editor has focus, one ready displayed entry allows shortcut copy without text selection; multiple entries without text selection leave the clipboard unchanged and prompt the user to choose. A click targets an entry. Numeric result copy omits its unit while preserving displayed numeric formatting; dropping units for copying does not merge display entries or discard hidden meanings. In quick mode, Enter or modified-Enter with multiple answers first focuses this row and highlights the first entry without copying or recording. Left/Right navigate and reveal the focused entry through horizontal scrolling; a later confirmation command acts on that entry. Escape restores the formula cursor. A click remains copy-only and returns focus to input. These commands were accepted in copying round 6. Round 14 adds Ctrl+C/Cmd+C while this row has focus: copy the highlighted ready answer and keep focus and selection there, regardless of an inactive editor text selection. Typing, paste, Backspace and Delete end selection and perform the usual edit at the restored formula cursor/selection with live recalculation and no copy or confirmation. Round 15 accepts Left/Right stopping at row boundaries without wrapping, and Up/Down ending selection and immediately performing ordinary history navigation without copying or confirming. Round 16 fixes ordering for the known metre/minute ambiguity: metre before minute, ambiguous occurrences left to right; filtering preserves relative order and a grouped display stays at the first constituent position. Numeric magnitude and UI language do not reorder these answers. Other ambiguity kinds need an explicit ordering rule if included later. Other remaining keys, exact focus styling and screen-reader announcements still need decisions or prototype verification.
result.alternatives.label.location: Single horizontal scrollable result row beneath the fixed input, containing values and unit symbols without interpretation captions.

error.unsupportedUnit.meaning: Explains that no valid answer with a supported final unit remains.
error.unsupportedUnit.context: Accepted in contextual-units round 4. Final unit support is checked after cancellation; only interpretations with unsupported final units are discarded. Policies for other mathematical errors remain open. Use the accepted result ordering for known metre/minute ambiguity and the separate accepted copy/confirmation contracts; ordering for any later added ambiguity must be specified explicitly. Supported compound families are speed, pace and information-transfer rate; area and volume remain supported. Examples of excluded final units are kg*m, s² and m/s². Diagnostic precedence when other errors also occur is still undecided.
error.unsupportedUnit.location: Calculation diagnostic region when no valid supported-unit answer remains after final cancellation and interpretation filtering.

help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.text: Supported compound units are speed (length/time, for example km/h), pace (time/length, min/km) and information-transfer rate (information/time, MB/s). Area and volume remain supported. Check support after final cancellation: (2s * 3s) / 1s = 6s is valid. Final units such as kg*m, s² and m/s² are excluded. Discard interpretations with unsupported final units and show the remaining valid answers; show the short unsupported-unit diagnostic only if no valid supported answer remains. Policies for other errors are still being specified. Temperature retains its separate conversion-only rule.
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.meaning: Defines the limited supported compound-unit families while retaining area and volume.
help.precedence.simpleCompoundUnits.context: Accepted in contextual-units round 4. Final unit support is checked after cancellation; only interpretations with unsupported final units are discarded. Policies for other mathematical errors remain open. Use the accepted result ordering for known metre/minute ambiguity and the separate accepted copy/confirmation contracts; ordering for any later added ambiguity must be specified explicitly. Temperature arithmetic is not added by intermediate-unit cancellation.

help.precedence.minHeading.meaning: Introduces the shared spelling of the minute alias and the minimum function.
help.precedence.minHeading.context: Help for argument-count disambiguation accepted through contextual-units round 5, including the implied coefficient and min/max minimum arity.
help.precedence.minHeading.location: After duration notation and before unit powers in operator help.

help.precedence.minRule.text: The min function takes at least two arguments separated by semicolons. One complete expression in the following parentheses denotes minutes multiplied by that expression: 2min(2+4) equals 12 minutes. With no coefficient, one minute is implied: min(2+4) = 1min(2+4), or 6 minutes. Two or more arguments denote the function: 2 min(2;4) = 2 * min(2;4) = 4, without a unit. Spaces before min do not change the meaning. Count arguments at the current parentheses level: 2min(max(2;4)) has one outer argument and equals 8 minutes. While 2min(2; is incomplete, the result stays blank. Closing it as 2min(2;) produces a missing-argument error, without reinterpreting the list as minutes. The max function also requires at least two arguments. Other malformed argument lists are still being specified.
help.precedence.minRule.meaning: Explains how min distinguishes the minute unit from the minimum function by its outer argument count, including an implied one-minute coefficient and missing-argument states.
help.precedence.minRule.context: Accepted through contextual-units round 5, superseding one-argument functions min and max. Nested-call separators do not count as outer arguments. The explicitly accepted incomplete min list has no live result, and the closed list with a missing argument is an error. Do not reinterpret it as a minute product. Minute examples express value and dimension, not a new default output spelling. Other malformed lists remain open; this rule does not automatically allow every unit without a coefficient.
help.precedence.minRule.location: Minutes and min function section of operator help and generated previews.

completion.function.min.description.text: Smallest of two or more values.
completion.function.min.description.meaning: Describes the minimum function and its required minimum argument count.
completion.function.min.description.context: Shown when suggesting the min function, whose arguments are separated by semicolons. Contextual-units round 4 changes its minimum arity to two. Unit-alias min is a separate interpretation; this entry describes the function.
completion.function.min.description.location: Immediately after the complete min signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Use the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without right-edge alignment.

error.missingArgument.meaning: Explains that an argument position in a closed argument list is empty.
error.missingArgument.context: Approved in contextual-units round 5 for a closed list such as 2min(2;). The incomplete 2min(2; keeps the result blank instead. A closed list with a missing argument must not be reinterpreted as a minute quantity. Other malformed lists and diagnostic precedence remain to be specified.
error.missingArgument.location: The calculation diagnostic region associated with the current expression.

completion.function.max.description.text: Largest of two or more values.
completion.function.max.description.meaning: Describes the maximum function and its required minimum argument count.
completion.function.max.description.context: Shown when suggesting the max function, whose arguments are separated by semicolons. Contextual-units round 5 changes its minimum arity to two. No unit named max is introduced.
completion.function.max.description.location: Immediately after the complete max signature in the same suggestion row, separated by a gap. Use the same font size, lighter weight and reduced opacity, without right-edge alignment.

error.missingOperator.meaning: Explains that an explicit operation is needed between the adjacent quantities.

The behavior is approved; the exact wording is an editorial draft. Do not use this error to reject the accepted ambiguous 1m30m readings, incomplete 1h30, or other supported implicit multiplication. Diagnostic precedence for unrelated errors remains open.

help.copy.quickRule.text: In the quick-mode formula editor with no text selected, press {shortcut} to copy the only displayed current result. With text selected, the shortcut copies that selection, including its unit text. Click a result to copy it. When several results are displayed, the editor has focus and no text is selected, the shortcut leaves the clipboard unchanged and prompts you to choose a result. The calculator stays open, your formula and cursor are preserved, and focus returns to input after a click. Quick copy does not add a history entry. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.copy.quickRule.meaning: Explains numeric-only result copying, text-selection precedence, the single-entry shortcut condition and choosing among several displayed results.
help.copy.quickRule.context: Accepted through copying round 2. Supply Ctrl+C on Windows and Cmd+C on macOS. A result must be ready and current. A single displayed entry can group several hidden meanings or rounded working values; copying its displayed number does not choose a hidden interpretation. Count the entire grouped result row, including entries outside the horizontal viewport. With editor focus and multiple entries without text selection, preserve the clipboard and show copy.chooseResult. Unit omission applies to numeric quick-copy results, not selected formula text. Numeric prefixes are not units; localized logical results retain their previously approved displayed text. Keyboard selection for confirmation is described in help.confirm.multipleRule. Round 14 accepts copying the highlighted answer while focus is already in the current result row; see help.copy.focusedResultRule. Text-selection precedence in this paragraph applies only while the editor has focus. Known metre/minute result ordering is accepted in round 16; see help.results.orderRule. Feedback geometry remains to be verified. This fragment does not add interpretation captions. This paragraph is scoped to quick-mode editor focus. Round 18 accepts the separate current-expression target and result-row commands in expanded sheets; see help.sheet.copyRule. Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers. Round 24 adds calendar answers: copy the complete displayed date/time/day-carry/offset text, not a numeric timestamp or a unitless date component. Selected source text stays literal, saved history stays immutable, and dynamic copy/confirmation uses the coherent ready result set already shown. Round 25 copies the complete displayed calendar period with units and both calendar/fixed parts. When the calendar-month component normalizes to zero, it is an ordinary fixed duration and retains numeric-coefficient-only copy. This does not change physical-quantity copy or the percentage fraction exception. Round 27 accepts approximately zero as a ready result. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. Exact zero and approximate zero are distinct display entries; identical approximate entries group while retaining every latent value. Multiple visible entries still require choosing. Selected source text remains literal. Typed computation preserves the working value and its type. Copy uses the displayed coefficient under the existing rule. Round 30 accepts choosing among expression scales by fewest fractional decimal places at working precision before screen rounding, ignoring insignificant trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit scale. Preserve a sole scale, including after functions: floor(1234mm) displays 1000mm; 90s remains 90s. Apply across ordinary measurements, information, fixed duration and derived numerators. Inherit scale context through names/functions; min/max keep selected-value context. Full ladders apply only without scale context. Preserve working values, types, explicit targets and saved historical displays; see language/unit-display.json.

Do not show it for selected formula text or to reinterpret a missing/stale result as a valid answer. Keyboard confirmation selection is now specified in help.confirm.multipleRule. help.confirm.retryRule.text: If confirmation fails, retry without changing the formula, result or chosen answer to finish the same calculation. The pending quick calculation keeps the same clock snapshot. Escape cancels the wait, keeps the window open and refreshes the calculation; editing also cancels. Saved history remains. Hiding and reopening preserves the wait within the session. Ordinary copy failures and sheet copying do not freeze the calculation.

help.confirm.multipleRule.text: When quick mode shows several results, press {confirmShortcut} or {hideShortcut} to focus the result row. The first answer is highlighted, but nothing is copied or saved yet. Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow to choose; the row scrolls when needed and stops at either end without wrapping. Up Arrow and Down Arrow leave result selection and immediately navigate history as usual, without copying or confirming. Press {confirmShortcut} again to record the calculation and copy the chosen answer, then start empty input with history collapsed. Press {hideShortcut} instead to confirm and hide the calculator. Escape returns the cursor to its previous position in the formula without changes. Clicking an answer still only copies it and returns focus to input. Typing, pasting, Backspace or Delete returns you to the formula at the previous cursor or text selection and performs the usual edit. This ends result selection and recalculates without copying or recording; Backspace and Delete edit formula text, not history.

help.history.recordRule.text: History keeps the formula, all its results and the answer chosen when you confirmed the calculation. Copying one answer does not remove the others. Saved results do not change when you edit a constant or function. When you bring a formula back into input, it is calculated again using the current definitions; the original history entry stays unchanged. Bringing a formula back into input does not itself add a new history entry. Each new successful confirmation adds a separate history entry, even for an identical calculation. Retrying an unfinished confirmation after an error does not duplicate its saved entry. If a saved definition was renamed, recalling its formula uses the current name of that same definition; the original history text and answers remain unchanged. After a definition is deleted, recalculation may require restoring it or correcting the formula.
help.history.recordRule.meaning: Explains what a history record retains and distinguishes viewing saved results from recalculating a recalled formula.
help.history.recordRule.context: Accepted in copying round 7. Records retain working values and hidden interpretations as well as the displayed answer chosen at confirmation, not merely the rounded unitless clipboard text. Historical values are not recalculated when definitions change; recalling a formula into input uses current definitions. Copying round 8 accepts a row containing the formula and all saved displayed results, with the confirmation choice in bold and horizontal overflow; see help.history.displayRule. Every new successful confirmation creates a separate entry even for identical content; retrying an unfinished confirmation after failure must not duplicate its entry. This does not approve a new badge or button, automatic restoration of old definitions, or a serialization format. Under round 16, an unchanged retry also requires the same chosen displayed answer. Confirming a different answer after partial failure creates a new entry and preserves any entry already saved with the previous choice. Round 18 accepts semantic rename handling on structured recall into quick input or a sheet: preserve the historical source text and values, but adapt references to the current name of the same definition. Reusing its former name for another definition must not hijack that binding. Ordinary selected-text copying retains visible original text. History alone does not block deletion of a global definition; no automatic substitution of an unrelated same-named replacement is approved.
help.history.recordRule.location: History section of application help, alongside the explanation of recalling calculations. Documentation text; the history row and its accessible presentation are specified separately.

history.result.chosen.meaning: Identifies the historical answer selected when the calculation was confirmed.

It describes the original confirmation choice, not current keyboard focus or a later click. No visible interpretation caption or badge is added. Exact native announcement and integration with the full history entry require prototype verification.

help.history.displayRule.text: Each history row shows the formula and all its saved results. With several results, the answer chosen at confirmation is bold. Long rows scroll horizontally. Moving through history does not change the saved choice.
help.history.displayRule.meaning: Explains the history row, its saved choice emphasis and access to long content.
help.history.displayRule.context: Accepted in copying round 8. All saved displayed answers are shown after the existing grouping of identical full formatted answers, retaining hidden interpretations. Interpretation captions remain absent. A single displayed answer needs no additional choice emphasis. Bold emphasis must preserve the existing dim fractional tail. Saved choice is distinct from current keyboard focus. Exact visual styling and accessibility remain subject to prototype verification. Clicking a saved answer copies it under the rule accepted in round 15; see help.history.copyRule. history.undo.meaning: Restores the most recent history deletion or whole-history clearing operation that has not yet been undone.
history.undo.context: Copying round 10 accepts undoing deletions in reverse order until the application fully exits, including whole-history clearing as one operation. Undo from the previous session is unavailable after a full exit. This is separate from formula text undo. Accepted in copying rounds 9 and 10. Undo has no short timer while the application remains running. Copying round 13 places this action in the shared history menu. It requires an undoable deletion or clear from the current session and can remain available when the history is empty. Menu geometry, failure feedback and exact unavailable presentation still require verification; this does not assign formula editor undo shortcuts to history.
history.undo.location: Item in the shared history menu; applies to undoable history operations rather than the current formula text.

history.clear.description.text: This will clear your calculation history. Your constants, functions, sheets and templates will be kept. You can undo the clearing until you fully quit the application.
history.clear.description.meaning: Explains the scope of clearing history and the other data that will be preserved.
history.clear.description.context: Editorial text for the whole-history confirmation accepted in copying round 9. Shown with history.clear.title before confirmation. Copying round 10 accepts undoing clearing until the application fully exits, including after the window is hidden and reopened. Do not promise Undo after a full exit or erase newer calculations when undoing a clear.
history.clear.description.location: Body of the calculation-history clearing confirmation dialog.

history.clear.confirm.meaning: Confirms the pending request to clear the entire calculation history.
history.clear.confirm.context: Primary confirmation action in the history-clearing dialog accepted in copying round 9. help.history.searchRule.text: In quick mode, press {shortcut} to search history by formula or saved result. Type any part of a formula or saved displayed result; matching ignores letter case. Enter closes search and brings the chosen formula into input for recalculation without confirming or copying it. Escape closes search and restores your previous formula and cursor. With no matches, Enter recalls nothing. The formula input stays in place, and searching does not recalculate saved results.
help.history.searchRule.meaning: Explains opening history search while preserving the current formula draft.

Copying round 11 accepts case-insensitive substring matching in the formula or any saved displayed result. Matches retain the normal history order; an empty query shows the entire history. This does not change case-sensitive expression semantics or recalculate saved values. Preserve ordinary substring matches and stored text. Do not normalize caret exponentiation into unit shorthand, rewrite names/comments, evaluate formulas or convert units/bases. help.history.manageRule.text: Deleting one history entry requires no confirmation. Clearing the entire history requires confirmation. Restoring removed entries keeps calculations added later. These actions preserve your constants, functions, sheets and templates. History Undo is separate from undoing formula text edits.

help.history.manageRule.context: Accepted in copying rounds 9 and 10. Deletion targets a specific record rather than matching content. Undo restores complete records with working values, hidden interpretations and the original chosen answer in their former order. Full-history clearing is undone as one operation without deleting newer records. Undo remains available while the application runs, without a short timer; no previous-session Undo is promised after full exit. Ctrl+Z/Cmd+Z in the formula editor continue to undo text only. Copying round 11 accepts keeping the entire history across launches until manual deletion, without age or record-count expiry. This retention is separate from session-limited Undo. Copying round 13 supplies control access through the shared history menu; see help.history.menuRule. Menu presentation and error behavior remain open.
help.history.manageRule.location: History management section of application help.

help.history.retentionRule.text: Your history is kept between application launches until you delete it. Old entries are not removed automatically because of their age or the number of saved calculations. Undo for deletions and clearing is available only until you fully quit the application.
help.history.retentionRule.meaning: Explains durable history retention and distinguishes it from the shorter availability of deletion Undo.
help.history.retentionRule.context: Accepted in copying round 11. The entire history is retained without automatic age or record-count cleanup; manually deleted records do not reappear on an ordinary relaunch. This does not select a storage format, require loading all records into memory, or promise recovery of deleted records after exit.
help.history.retentionRule.location: History section of application help, next to history management and Undo rules.

help.history.searchNotationRule.text: History search treats 1,5 and 1.5, and 1000 and 1 000, as equivalent number spellings. help.history.navigationRule.text: In quick mode, Up Arrow opens history and immediately brings the preceding calculation into input. Press Up again to recall older entries while the list moves downward through the fixed input. Down Arrow moves back through the entries until it restores the text you had before browsing, even if that text was not empty. Recalled formulas are calculated again using the current definitions; saved history entries stay unchanged. Returning to your original input restores its cursor and collapses history. Up stops at the oldest entry, and further Down at your original input does not clear it.
help.history.navigationRule.meaning: Explains direct console history recall and returning to the original quick input.
help.history.navigationRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16 as the user replacement for the proposed Tab history-view mode. Preserve the original text and cursor/selection from the start of browsing; repeated recalls do not overwrite that navigation snapshot. An open completion menu retains its existing arrow priority. Recall and return are text-undo steps under help.input.undoRule and do not confirm, copy or add history. The saved record is unchanged. The previous unconditional empty-input return is superseded. Round 17 accepts collapse on return to any original input with cursor/selection restoration, Up stopping at the oldest entry, and Down preserving the original input once reached. This is quick-mode navigation; history search keeps its own accepted no-recall-until-Enter behavior.

help.input.undoRule.text: Each formula recalled from history and each Down Arrow return to your original input is one text-undo step. Press {shortcut} to restore the previous text and cursor; the formula is recalculated with the current definitions. This also applies when you use a search result or Use formula. A new empty input after successful confirmation starts a separate undo chain. Undo does not remove saved calculations or undo a clipboard copy. Hiding the window keeps text undo available; fully quitting ends that chain. Copying a sheet result does not start a new text-undo chain.
help.input.undoRule.meaning: Explains text undo for history recall and its boundary between confirmed quick calculations and application sessions.
help.input.undoRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, points 1-3, with the direct original-input return correction from point 5 taking precedence over the old unconditional empty return. Use Ctrl+Z on Windows and Cmd+Z on macOS. Restore the prior text and cursor/selection as one undo step for each recall or actual original-input return. Merely selecting a search result does not mutate input. Revisiting a history entry recalls its saved formula; unsaved edits can be recovered through text undo. This does not alter the separate undo of history deletions. Only full successful confirmation starts the next calculation and new undo chain; a partial failure does not. Extended-sheet editing and crash recovery are separate decisions. Round 17 separately accepts inserting a historical formula into an expanded sheet as one ordinary editing action; see help.history.extendedShortcutRule. This does not apply quick-mode confirmation resets to sheet editing. Round 18 explicitly keeps the sheet text-undo chain when copying results. help.quick.restoreRule.text: After you fully quit and reopen the application, quick mode restores your last input and cursor, with history collapsed and focus in the input. The formula is calculated again using the current definitions. If your last input was empty, it stays empty. Text undo from the previous application session is not restored. Simply hiding and reopening the window keeps the current text-undo chain.
help.quick.restoreRule.meaning: Explains normal-restart persistence of quick input separately from text undo.
help.quick.restoreRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, point 3. Persist the last quick-input text and cursor/selection for normal full exit and restart. Recalculate restored input with current definitions and normal incomplete/error behavior; do not expose a stored old result as a newly ready answer. Start with history collapsed, editor focus and no restored result-selection, search or menu state. This does not decide crash recovery, persistence of the original-input navigation snapshot during interrupted browsing, or the lifecycle of calculation sheets. Ordinary window hiding is not a full application exit.
