This does not automatically persist prior-session undo or choose navigation-snapshot serialization.
help.quick.restoreRule.location: Application lifecycle and quick-input sections of help; no launch dialog or new visible control is added.

help.results.orderRule.text: Possible answers follow a fixed interpretation order. For m, metre comes before minute; ambiguous occurrences are considered from left to right. Thus 10m / 2s shows 5m/s before 300. Removing invalid alternatives keeps the remaining order; identical displayed answers share the position of their first alternative. Changing numbers or the interface language does not sort answers into a different order.
help.results.orderRule.meaning: Explains stable ordering and first-position display grouping for the accepted metre/minute ambiguity.
help.results.orderRule.context: Accepted in copying round 16, point 4. Known ambiguous occurrences use metre before minute and occur left to right in source; combinations follow the corresponding sequential interpretation order. Filtering preserves relative order and grouping uses the first constituent position while preserving all hidden meanings and working values. The Russian alias follows the same identity order. This is a presentation contract, not a mandated evaluation algorithm or a choice of one hidden interpretation. Source changes may change the alternatives; other ambiguity kinds require an explicit ordering extension if later included. Existing no-caption and horizontal-overflow rules remain in effect.
help.results.orderRule.location: Result interpretation section of application help, next to grouping and alternative-answer explanations. No visible ranking number or interpretation caption is added.

help.history.extendedShortcutRule.text: In expanded mode, press {shortcut} with either modifier key to open history while keeping your sheet unchanged. Up Arrow and Down Arrow choose a record; Left Arrow and Right Arrow choose its saved answer. Start at the latest record and its answer chosen at confirmation; when you change records, select that record’s confirmation choice. Navigation stops at the ends and scrolls the selected item into view. Press {copyShortcut} to copy the saved answer without recalculation and keep focus in history. Enter closes history and inserts the formula at your previous cursor, replacing selected text, as one ordinary edit. The sheet recalculates without confirming or adding history. Escape or {shortcut} again closes history without insertion and restores the previous cursor. Empty history provides nothing to select or insert. Ordinary arrows retain text-editor behavior while editing. References to renamed saved definitions use their current names in the inserted formula; the history record stays unchanged. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.meaning: Explains opening, navigating, copying and inserting from history while preserving the expanded sheet until insertion.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.context: Alt+Up with either physical modifier was accepted in round 16; the complete interaction was accepted in round 17, point 2. Use platform Alt/Option naming and Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS. Opening transfers focus to history while retaining sheet text and cursor/selection. Preserve saved record values and confirmation choices; navigation focus is not a stored-choice mutation. Use the existing numeric displayed text without units and localized logical text for clipboard copy; copying retains history focus and does not recalculate. Enter inserts the saved formula text at the retained cursor or replaces the retained selection in one ordinary edit, closes history, returns editor focus and triggers normal sheet recalculation without confirming or recording. An insertion producing incomplete or invalid input follows ordinary evaluation rules and does not reuse stale answers. Escape or repeated Alt+Up closes without insertion. Empty history cannot target a nonexistent record. This is a separate context from quick console recall, history search and completion navigation. Native focus, placement and accessibility remain to be verified. Per-line results, sheet autosave and local shadowing of global constants were accepted separately in points 4-6; see the sheet help fragments. Copying a newly calculated sheet result was accepted in round 18; see help.sheet.copyRule. Structured history insertion adapts references to renamed saved definitions to their current names while preserving the original history record, under help.definitions.renameRule. Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers. Round 24 adds calendar answers: copy the complete displayed date/time/day-carry/offset text, not a numeric timestamp or a unitless date component. Selected source text stays literal, saved history stays immutable, and dynamic copy/confirmation uses the coherent ready result set already shown. Round 25 copies the complete displayed calendar period with units and both calendar/fixed parts. When the calendar-month component normalizes to zero, it is an ordinary fixed duration and retains numeric-coefficient-only copy. This does not change physical-quantity copy or the percentage fraction exception. Round 27 accepts approximately zero as a ready result. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. Exact zero and approximate zero are distinct display entries; identical approximate entries group while retaining every latent value. Multiple visible entries still require choosing. Selected source text remains literal.
help.history.extendedShortcutRule.location: Expanded-mode keyboard help, alongside the history-opening action. The final help entry point and history placement remain interface work.

placeholders.shortcut: The accepted Alt+Up Arrow history-opening shortcut in platform display form, using the platform Alt/Option key name and accepting either physical modifier key.
placeholders.copyShortcut: The platform-specific result-copy shortcut: Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS.

help.sheet.dependenciesRule.text: In a calculation sheet, define each local variable once. Expressions may reference definitions farther down the sheet: total = price * quantity can precede price = 100 and quantity = 3 and still gives 300. Editing a definition recalculates its dependent expressions. Defining the same local name again is an error. Circular dependencies block the expressions in the cycle and those that depend on them; independent expressions still calculate. Multiline user-function bodies keep their sequential execution rules.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.meaning: Explains the accepted dependency model for sheet variables and its scope relative to function bodies.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 3. One sheet-local definition per name, forward references permitted, dependency-driven recalculation and explicit cycle handling. Reject duplicate local definitions rather than silently choosing first or last. Do not mark nonparticipating downstream expressions as themselves cyclic; they are blocked by a required value. Example identifiers may be localized in explanatory prose and do not create reserved names. Points 4-6 were subsequently accepted for sheets: see help.sheet.resultsRule, help.sheet.scopeRule and help.sheet.autosaveRule. These are separate from sequential function bodies and explicit global-definition saving. Global definition storage, name resolution and function dependencies remain their own domain contracts within the shared calculation core.
help.sheet.dependenciesRule.location: Calculation-sheet language section of application help, distinct from the sequential user-function body explanation.

sheet.duplicateVariable.text: Variable {name} is defined more than once in this sheet.
sheet.duplicateVariable.meaning: Reports a duplicate local variable definition in a calculation sheet.
sheet.duplicateVariable.context: Editorial wording for the duplicate-definition error accepted in round 17, point 3. Use when a sheet contains more than one local definition of the same name under the accepted case-sensitive naming rules. Do not reinterpret the duplicate as a sequential reassignment. This is not a rule rejecting a same-named global constant; point 5 now accepts sheet-local shadowing of a saved constant without changing that constant. Round 18 separately rejects sheet-local names matching saved user functions; use sheet.functionNameConflict for that case. It does not govern editing or saving a global definition or assignment inside a sequential function body.
sheet.duplicateVariable.location: Diagnostic associated with duplicate definitions in the calculation-sheet editor; exact highlighting and accessible announcement remain interface work.

placeholders.name: The duplicate sheet-local variable name as written by the user; preserve its spelling and case.

sheet.dependencyError.text: A required value could not be calculated.
sheet.dependencyError.meaning: Explains why a sheet expression cannot calculate when a required dependency is blocked.
sheet.dependencyError.context: Editorial wording for an expression blocked by a required dependency under rounds 17 and 18. A dependency with an error or incomplete input has no ready value; do not show a stale value as current. A downstream expression need not itself participate in a cycle. Independent expressions continue calculating. Do not present transient incomplete input itself as a mathematical error; the affected incomplete expression has no ready answer. Preserve lazy if/and/or behavior for unused branches. Recovery of expression boundaries after malformed syntax and conditional-cycle analysis remain technical language work.
sheet.dependencyError.location: Diagnostic associated with a sheet expression that cannot obtain a required dependency; exact presentation remains interface work.

help.sheet.resultsRule.text: Each completed expression or assignment in a calculation sheet shows its own result. For example, price = 100 shows 100 and price * 3 shows 300. Blank lines and comments have no result. If an expression has several valid answers, show them all using the existing grouping, ordering and horizontal-scrolling rules.
help.sheet.resultsRule.meaning: Explains results for each calculable sheet expression or assignment.
help.sheet.resultsRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 4 after scope clarification. This applies to expanded sheets, not intermediate statements inside a saved function body. Preserve all underlying meanings and working values when displayed answers are grouped. A completed but invalid expression must not expose a stale ready answer. Copy commands were accepted in round 18; see help.sheet.copyRule. Exact placement and font treatment remain interface work; this paragraph does not approve a right-hand result column.
help.sheet.resultsRule.location: Expanded-sheet result section of application help, near the sheet dependency explanation. The visual placement of per-expression results still requires prototype review.

help.sheet.scopeRule.text: Local variables belong to their calculation sheet. They do not become saved definitions in quick mode or other sheets. A local variable takes precedence over a saved constant with the same name inside that sheet without changing the saved constant. If the global price is 50 and a sheet defines price = 100, that sheet uses 100 while quick mode still uses 50. Built-in names remain protected. A sheet-local name cannot match a saved function name. Saved functions do not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables.
help.sheet.scopeRule.meaning: Explains sheet-local variable scope and shadowing of a saved user constant.
help.sheet.scopeRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 5 after scope clarification. Global saved constants are not overwritten by sheet editing or autosave. Existing built-in identifier protection remains unchanged. Example names may be localized in help prose without changing users’ identifiers. Round 18 accepts an error for sheet-local names matching saved functions and the saved-function environment of parameters, own sequential local intermediates and saved global definitions. Arguments evaluate in the caller context before binding. See help.definitions.functionScopeRule and help.definitions.namesRule. This does not impose global uniqueness on every function parameter or local intermediate.
help.sheet.scopeRule.location: Expanded-sheet variable section of application help, distinct from the saved-definition library help.

help.sheet.autosaveRule.text: You can keep several named calculation sheets. Their text is saved automatically on this computer, including unfinished or erroneous expressions. Autosaving does not add calculation-history entries. Reopening a sheet restores its text and calculates it again using the current saved constants and functions. Saving a template and saving a global constant or function remain separate actions.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.meaning: Explains local autosave of named sheet documents and recalculation on reopening.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.context: Accepted in round 17, point 6 after scope clarification. Save sheet text independently of calculation success; the data model must distinguish a persisted erroneous draft from a failed persistence operation. Reopening does not present an old cached answer as a newly evaluated result. This behavior does not autosave or publish global definition edits and does not choose template update semantics. Exact storage format, management controls, persistence timing, retry and crash recovery remain architecture or product decisions; do not imply verified durability guarantees from this help paragraph.
help.sheet.autosaveRule.location: Sheet persistence section of application help, alongside named-sheet management. This explains automatic saving and does not introduce a manual Save sheet button.

help.sheet.copyRule.text: In the sheet editor, Enter inserts a new line. With text selected, {copyShortcut} copies the selection. Without a selection, it copies the only ready displayed answer of the expression containing the cursor. If that expression has several answers, the clipboard stays unchanged and you are prompted to choose a result. Click an answer to copy it. Press {resultShortcut} to copy the current expression’s single answer or focus its result row to choose with Left and Right. In that row, Enter or {resultShortcut} copies the chosen answer and returns to the previous editor cursor; {copyShortcut} copies it while keeping row focus. Escape returns without copying. Typing, paste, Backspace or Delete resumes normal editing at the previous cursor or selection. Numeric answers copy the displayed number without units, preserving shown rounding, digits, sign, grouping and base prefix and case. Logical answers copy their visible localized text. Missing, invalid or stale answers cannot be copied. The sheet stays open and is not cleared. Copying, recalculation and autosave do not add history entries or reset text undo. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3 according to your number-format locale. Calendar answers copy their complete shown date, time, day carry and any shown offset. A calendar period with a nonzero month component is also copied in full, including its units; an ordinary fixed duration still copies only its numeric coefficient. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.sheet.copyRule.meaning: Explains current-expression copying and result-row focus in an expanded calculation sheet.
help.sheet.copyRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 1. Supply Ctrl+C and Ctrl+Enter on Windows, Cmd+C and Cmd+Enter on macOS. Count the complete grouped displayed result set of the expression containing the editor cursor, including horizontal overflow, not all sheet results. Preserve underlying meanings when display entries group. Inactive editor selection does not override a focused answer row. The common history records quick-mode confirmations, not sheet copy or autosave. History opened by Alt+Up retains its separate Enter-for-insertion context. Do not inherit quick-mode clearing, hiding or confirmation undo resets. Other row keys, result placement and native focus still need design or verification. Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers. Round 24 adds calendar answers: copy the complete displayed date/time/day-carry/offset text, not a numeric timestamp or a unitless date component. Selected source text stays literal, saved history stays immutable, and dynamic copy/confirmation uses the coherent ready result set already shown. Round 25 copies the complete displayed calendar period with units and both calendar/fixed parts. When the calendar-month component normalizes to zero, it is an ordinary fixed duration and retains numeric-coefficient-only copy. This does not change physical-quantity copy or the percentage fraction exception. Round 27 accepts approximately zero as a ready result. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. Exact zero and approximate zero are distinct display entries; identical approximate entries group while retaining every latent value. Multiple visible entries still require choosing. Selected source text remains literal. Typed computation preserves the working value and its type. Copy uses the displayed coefficient under the existing rule. Round 30 accepts choosing among expression scales by fewest fractional decimal places at working precision before screen rounding, ignoring insignificant trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit scale. Preserve a sole scale, including after functions: floor(1234mm) displays 1000mm; 90s remains 90s. Apply across ordinary measurements, information, fixed duration and derived numerators. Inherit scale context through names/functions; min/max keep selected-value context. Full ladders apply only without scale context. Preserve working values, types, explicit targets and saved historical displays; see language/unit-display.json.
help.sheet.copyRule.location: Expanded-sheet copying section of application help; not a new permanent control in the editor.

placeholders.copyShortcut: Platform copy command: Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on macOS.
placeholders.resultShortcut: Platform sheet-result command: Ctrl+Enter on Windows or Cmd+Enter on macOS.

help.sheet.errorRule.text: An expression with an error or incomplete input has no ready result. Expressions depending on it also have no ready answer; independent expressions continue calculating. For a = 1 / 0, b = a + 1 and c = 2 + 2, a has an error, b cannot obtain its dependency and c is 4. An unknown-name message identifies the name. Previous values are never presented as current results. The sheet still saves your text. Unused branches of if, and and or are not evaluated.
help.sheet.errorRule.meaning: Explains how sheet errors and incomplete values affect dependents while independent calculations remain available.
help.sheet.errorRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 2. Apply to distinguishable expressions and their dependencies. Incomplete input does not by itself warrant a mathematical error message; keep the ready result absent. Use expression.unknownName for unresolved names and sheet.dependencyError for a blocked required dependency. Parser recovery and conditional-cycle analysis remain technical design work.
help.sheet.errorRule.location: Expanded-sheet error and dependency section of application help.

help.definitions.functionScopeRule.text: A saved function uses its parameters, its own local intermediate names and saved global definitions. It does not implicitly use the calling sheet’s local variables. With global price = 50 and cost(x) = x * price, a sheet-local price = 100 does not change cost(2): the answer is 100. To use a sheet value inside a function, pass it as an argument. Arguments are calculated in the caller’s context before they bind to parameters. Multiline function bodies run in order.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.meaning: Explains the saved-function name environment and explicit passing of caller-local values.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 3. Preserve sheet-local shadowing of saved constants in direct sheet expressions, sequential function bodies and the last-expression return rule. Example identifiers may be localized in documentation, not by renaming user definitions. This is name scope; exact ambiguous-value propagation remains a separate language contract.
help.definitions.functionScopeRule.location: Saved-function section of application help, next to parameter and multiline examples.

help.definitions.constantRule.text: A saved constant retains its definition formula and its dependencies on other saved constants. With rate = 20% and factor = 1 + rate, explicitly saving rate as 10% changes factor to 1.1. Editing a draft does not change the saved definition before you save it. Cyclic definitions are not allowed.
help.definitions.constantRule.meaning: Explains live formula dependencies of saved constants and their explicit publication boundary.
help.definitions.constantRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 4. Do not freeze a constant to a rounded or unitless clipboard snapshot. Implementation storage and caching are unchosen. This paragraph does not settle propagation of ambiguous units or result sets through definitions.
help.definitions.constantRule.location: Saved-constant section of application help, alongside definition examples.

help.definitions.saveRule.text: Edit a saved definition as a draft, then choose Save to apply it. A valid saved change updates future calculations and recalculates current quick input and open dependent sheets. Invalid syntax, unknown references, recursion or cyclic dependencies keep the previous working version; your edits remain available to correct. A valid function may still fail for particular arguments: f(x) = 1 / x fails at zero. The description from the header’s first # comment is saved with the definition. Existing history answers do not recalculate.
help.definitions.saveRule.meaning: Explains draft editing, explicit publication, validation failures and affected calculations.
help.definitions.saveRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 5. Reuse common.save for the explicit Save command. Header descriptions remain derived from the definition text, not an independently autosaved field. Validation is not exhaustive evaluation for all arguments. Disk-failure behavior and publication atomicity still require technical design. Do not treat sheet autosave as permission to publish global definitions.
help.definitions.saveRule.location: Saved-definition editing section of application help.

help.definitions.namesRule.text: Each global name identifies one saved constant or function. Functions cannot share a name by accepting different numbers of arguments. Creating a definition does not overwrite an existing one; open it explicitly to edit. A sheet-local variable may shadow a saved constant, but it cannot use a saved function’s name. Built-in names remain protected.
help.definitions.namesRule.meaning: Explains global definition uniqueness, explicit editing and sheet-local name conflicts.
help.definitions.namesRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 6, under the existing case-sensitive identifier rules. This does not impose global uniqueness on parameters or intermediate locals belonging to separate function bodies. Function-body local conflict details remain part of language design.
help.definitions.namesRule.location: Naming section of saved-definition help, with a reference from sheet-variable help.

help.definitions.renameRule.text: Renaming a saved definition updates references to it in other saved definitions, sheets and templates. Unrelated local names and comments are unchanged. History keeps its original formula and answers; recalling the formula for a new calculation uses the definition’s current name. Renaming price to cost leaves price * 2 in history but recalls cost * 2. Reusing the old name for another definition does not redirect those references. Name conflicts are checked before the rename; a rename cannot be partially applied.
help.definitions.renameRule.meaning: Explains semantic rename propagation while preserving historical source text and values.
help.definitions.renameRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 7. Update references bound to the definition, not plain string matches, homonymous locals, comments or arbitrary text. Apply adapting recall through console history, history search, Use formula and sheet insertion. Ordinary copied selected historical text stays as visibly written. Validate target conflicts before mutation. Stable identifiers, partial-document bindings and atomic storage require architecture work; the help states intended behavior, not completed verification.
help.definitions.renameRule.location: Rename section of saved-definition management help.

help.definitions.deleteRule.text: A definition cannot be deleted while other saved definitions, sheets or templates use it; the calculator shows where it is used. History alone does not prevent deletion and retains its saved answers. Recalculating an old formula may require restoring the definition or correcting the formula. An unused definition is deleted without an extra confirmation dialog and can be restored with the definition library’s Undo until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps Undo available. If a new definition now uses the same name, restoration reports the conflict and does not overwrite the new data.
help.definitions.deleteRule.meaning: Explains deletion blockers, historical independence and session-limited library deletion Undo.
help.definitions.deleteRule.context: Accepted in round 18, point 8. Definition deletion Undo is distinct from editor text undo and history deletion Undo. History does not keep a definition undeletable, but semantic identity must not be silently hijacked by an unrelated replacement when recalculating. Exact action access, storage and errors remain design work; do not infer additional blocker categories for unsaved quick input or global draft edits.
help.definitions.deleteRule.location: Delete and restore section of saved-definition management help.

definitions.rename.meaning: Names the command that renames a saved definition and its semantic references.
definitions.rename.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.rename.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.delete.meaning: Names the deletion command for a saved constant or function.
definitions.delete.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.delete.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.undo.meaning: Names the separate library command that restores a deleted definition.
definitions.undo.context: Editorial command wording for behavior accepted in round 18. Apply the corresponding rename, usage-blocking or session-limited restore rules. This entry does not approve a new permanent editor button or extend text/history Undo. Round 19 places access to definition management in the shared library; accepted definition usage and Undo rules remain unchanged.
definitions.undo.location: Saved-definition actions accessed through the shared library; exact menu/control placement remains interface work.

definitions.inUse.text: {name} is used by other definitions, sheets or templates.
definitions.inUse.meaning: Explains why a saved definition cannot be deleted.
definitions.inUse.context: Show with the actual usage locations when round-18 deletion is blocked. History alone must not trigger this message.
definitions.inUse.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The saved definition name; preserve its user-provided spelling and case.

definitions.nameConflict.text: The name {name} is already used by a saved definition.
definitions.nameConflict.meaning: Reports a conflict when creating or renaming a global definition.
definitions.nameConflict.context: Round 18 permits one saved definition per case-sensitive global name, with no constant/function collision or overload by argument count. Do not overwrite existing data.
definitions.nameConflict.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The conflicting global definition name; preserve its spelling and case.

definitions.invalid.text: The definition has errors. Your edits are kept; the working version is unchanged.
definitions.invalid.meaning: Explains rejection of an invalid definition draft without losing editable text.
definitions.invalid.context: For editing an existing definition under round 18. Show the specific syntax, unknown-name, recursion or cycle diagnostic alongside this summary. Kept edits do not imply persisted crash recovery or successful disk storage. For a new invalid definition use its specific diagnostic, not a claim of an existing working version.
definitions.invalid.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

definitions.restoreConflict.text: Cannot restore {name}: a new definition uses that name.
definitions.restoreConflict.meaning: Explains why deletion Undo cannot restore without a name conflict.
definitions.restoreConflict.context: Accepted round-18 restore conflict: retain the new definition and do not silently overwrite it. The exact way to resolve the conflict remains interface work.
definitions.restoreConflict.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The name of the deleted definition being restored; preserve its original spelling and case.

sheet.functionNameConflict.text: {name} is a saved function name and cannot be a sheet variable.
sheet.functionNameConflict.meaning: Reports a sheet-local variable name colliding with a user function.
sheet.functionNameConflict.context: Accepted in round 18, point 6. Do not use for shadowing a saved constant, which is allowed, or as a global uniqueness restriction on all function-body intermediates.
sheet.functionNameConflict.location: Diagnostic beside the affected definition or sheet expression; exact visual and accessible presentation remains interface work.

placeholders.name: The conflicting sheet-local identifier, preserving its written spelling and case.

help.library.rule.text: Press {shortcut} inside the calculator to find sheets, templates and saved definitions in one library, grouped by type. Search by name; definitions can also be found by their descriptions from # comments. Enter opens a sheet, starts a template or opens a definition for editing. Creation and management actions are available here too.
help.library.rule.meaning: Explains shared access to saved objects through the local library command.
help.library.rule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 1. Use Ctrl+K on Windows and Cmd+K on macOS while the calculator is active. This is distinct from the configurable global invocation shortcut. Do not translate user names or descriptions. Exact library geometry, remaining key contexts, focus and native shortcut behavior require design or verification.
help.library.rule.location: Saved-object navigation section of application help.

placeholders.shortcut: The local library shortcut: Ctrl+K on Windows or Cmd+K on macOS.

help.templates.rule.text: Save a copy of a sheet as a template and choose its local parameter variables and default values. Starting the template with parameter values creates an independent named sheet with autosave. Editing that sheet does not change the template. Updating the template is explicit and does not rewrite sheets already created from it. References to saved global constants and functions remain live.
help.templates.rule.meaning: Explains templates as parameterized sources for independent calculation sheets.
help.templates.rule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 2. Do not turn template parameters into global definitions or freeze live global references into numeric snapshots. Round 20 accepts compact parameter fields prefilled with defaults, the ordinary expression language and validation before creating a sheet; see help.templates.parametersRule. Exact geometry remains interface work.
help.templates.rule.location: Template creation and reuse section of application help.

help.documents.manageRule.text: Create, rename, duplicate or delete sheets and templates from their management actions. Closing a sheet keeps it saved; a duplicate has its own text. Deleting one document does not require an extra confirmation dialog and can be undone until you fully quit. Hiding the window keeps document deletion Undo available. Other documents, history and definitions are preserved, and restoration does not overwrite newer data. This Undo is separate from text editing and history deletion Undo.
help.documents.manageRule.meaning: Explains document management, close-versus-delete behavior and the lifetime of document deletion Undo.
help.documents.manageRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 3. Preserve global definition deletion restrictions and its separate Undo. Round 20 accepts restoration of document text and semantic references without reverting global definitions; a missing dependency is diagnosed and an unrelated same-named definition must not replace it. See help.documents.restoreRule. Exact action access and naming-conflict presentation remain interface work.
help.documents.manageRule.location: Sheet and template management section of application help.

help.data.exportRule.text: A full export puts sheets, templates, saved definitions and shared settings such as theme, language and copy behavior into one portable file. History is not included and stays on this device. The global invocation shortcut, autostart and window placement also stay device-local. The file preserves calculation references, unit meanings and your own text for transfer between Windows and macOS. No account or cloud synchronization is required.
help.data.exportRule.meaning: Explains the accepted full transfer scope with history explicitly excluded.
help.data.exportRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 4 with the user correction. The request to remove history was interpreted in the export-scope context; it is not an instruction to erase local records or remove history as a feature. Device-local preferences are excluded from this package. Round 20 separately accepts full local backups including history and an unchecked-by-default Apply settings option during import; see the backup and import-settings help. Versioned serialization is required but its format is unchosen.
help.data.exportRule.location: Export section of data-management help, alongside full export.

help.data.selectedExportRule.text: Export selected sheets, templates or definitions together with the saved constants and functions they need, including further dependencies. Unrelated history and other data are not included. Incomplete sheet text can still be transferred; missing definitions are not invented.
help.data.selectedExportRule.meaning: Explains selected transfer with the necessary saved-definition dependency closure.
help.data.selectedExportRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 5. Include semantic dependencies, not merely text matches; preserve live definition identity and unit semantics. A document may contain incomplete or erroneous expressions without making its container invalid. Do not add unrelated history, account information or device settings to selected packages.
help.data.selectedExportRule.location: Selected export section of data-management help.

help.data.importRule.text: Preview additions and conflicts before importing. Importing the same unchanged object again does not duplicate it. A differing version that conflicts with an existing object is added as a separately named copy by default, with its internal references adjusted together. Existing objects are not overwritten. The file’s structure, version and reference integrity are checked before applying the import as one change. A damaged or unsupported file leaves your data unchanged. An incomplete sheet formula alone does not make the file damaged. Shared settings change only if you select Apply settings in the preview; the option starts unchecked.
help.data.importRule.meaning: Explains import preview, repeat-import behavior, conflict copies and all-or-nothing application.
help.data.importRule.context: Accepted in round 19, point 6, adjusted to the history-free export in point 4. Object identity and content comparison must preserve distinct objects; same-spelling names are not sufficient identity. Conflicting imported references must point to the intended imported or identical existing definition, not silently capture a different local one. Existing history remains local. Round 20 accepts an unchecked-by-default Apply settings option; show and apply common-setting changes only when selected. See help.data.importSettingsRule. help.finance.ratesRule.text: The convenient monthly forms use an annual nominal rate and a number of months: 12% annually means 1% for each calculation month. The general forms take a rate per period and a number of periods. Enter rates as ordinary expressions such as 12% or 0.12; the number 12 is not automatically interpreted as 12%. A zero rate is valid. An effective annual rate is not silently treated as a nominal rate, and financial months do not introduce calendar arithmetic.
help.finance.ratesRule.meaning: Explains accepted rate and period conventions for the two financial calculation forms.
help.finance.ratesRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. Approved monthly and periodic identifiers and positional signatures are in functions/catalog.json and ../language/financial-functions.json. The monthly rate is the annual nominal rate divided by 12. Rate conversion is explicit through effective and nominal. Financial months remain abstract rate/payment periods and do not introduce m as a month unit. Calendar input, dynamic names and the basic model are accepted in round 24. They do not change financial rate or payment-period conventions; calendar interval spellings are still pending.
help.finance.ratesRule.location: Financial help section covering rates and calculation periods.

help.finance.loanRule.text: A loan is fully repaid through equal periodic payments at a constant rate. Payments are at the end of each period by default; the beginning can be specified explicitly. Enter the loan amount as a positive amount; the returned payment is a positive amount too. Separate calculations provide the payment, total repayments and overpayment, which is total repayments minus the loan principal. At a zero rate, the payment is the loan amount divided by the number of payments. Fees and contract-specific rules are not added automatically.
help.finance.loanRule.meaning: Explains the accepted fully amortizing loan model and positive user-facing monetary magnitudes.
help.finance.loanRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. Positive principal, a positive integer count and a rate per period greater than -100% are required. The timing argument defaults to finance.timing.end; finance.timing.start is explicit. The accepted signatures map three separate metrics for each rate convention. Spreadsheet negative-cashflow input conventions are not inherited.

help.finance.savingsRule.text: Calculate savings from an initial amount, a constant rate and an equal contribution each period. The contribution is optional and defaults to zero; the initial amount may also be zero. Contributions occur at the end of the period by default, with the beginning available explicitly. Separate calculations return the accumulated amount and interest earned: the total minus the initial amount and all your contributions. At a zero rate, the total is simply the initial amount plus all contributions.
help.finance.savingsRule.meaning: Explains regular-contribution savings and separates growth from contributed money.
help.finance.savingsRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. Initial amount and contribution are nonnegative; the period count is a nonnegative integer. Contribution defaults to 0 and timing to finance.timing.end. To specify timing without a contribution, pass 0 explicitly in the contribution position. At zero periods, the total is the initial amount and earned interest is zero. A rate per period greater than -100% is required.
help.finance.savingsRule.location: Financial help section describing savings and compound growth.

help.finance.roiRule.text: Provide the total invested, including costs, and the total returned, including returned capital and additional receipts. Profit is returned money minus invested money. ROI is profit divided by investment, shown as a percentage for the whole period. Investing 100000 and receiving 130000 gives a profit of 30000 and ROI of 30%. Losses and negative ROI are valid, with no automatic annualization. ROI is undefined at zero investment; profit can still be calculated separately. Costs already included in investment are not subtracted again. Copying a percentage result uses its decimal fraction: 30% copies 0.3 or 0,3.
help.finance.roiRule.meaning: Explains whole-period profit and ROI with aggregated investment and return inputs.
help.finance.roiRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. profit and roi take total investment and total returned in this positional order. Both monetary inputs are nonnegative; roi requires positive investment. Returned money includes principal so costs are not subtracted twice. ROI is a percentage value, with the fraction as its numerical meaning and the accepted percentage behavior in expressions. Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers.
help.finance.roiRule.location: Financial help section describing profit and return on investment.

help.finance.paybackRule.text: Use the initial investment and a constant net cash inflow per period. Net cash flow is cash received minus cash paid. One calculation estimates a fractional payback time for cash arriving evenly within each period; another returns the number of complete periods when the entire payment arrives only at period end. An investment of 100000 with 30000 per period gives 10/3 periods or 4 complete periods, respectively. A positive investment with zero or negative net inflow does not pay back and has no ready numeric answer. With zero investment, either calculation returns zero periods.
help.finance.paybackRule.meaning: Explains the two explicit simple-payback models and the no-payback state.
help.finance.paybackRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. payback estimates fractional periods; payback_full returns a whole period count. Both take nonnegative initial investment and a constant net cash flow per period. Zero investment returns zero periods. Positive investment with nonpositive net cash flow has finance.notRepaid and no ready numeric answer. These functions are separate metrics, not ambiguous interpretations.
help.finance.paybackRule.location: Financial help section describing simple payback.

help.finance.precisionRule.text: Financial calculations use the same 30 significant digits and normal result display as other calculations. Each accrual or payment is not secretly rounded to cents. Use round(...; 2) explicitly when you want to round the final expression to two decimal places. Total repayments and earned interest are calculated from working values, not rounded text on screen. This does not create a contract-specific payment schedule with rounding at every step. Computed fractional results use 30 significant digits with exact ties rounded away from zero; subsequent operations use that working value.
help.finance.precisionRule.meaning: Explains shared precision and explicit final rounding in financial models.
help.finance.precisionRule.context: Accepted in round 21, point 6. Preserve the existing display precision and reduced-opacity fractional tail; no hidden financial display or per-payment cent rounding is introduced. round is an already accepted mathematical function, while the ellipsis denotes a documentation placeholder rather than literal parser syntax. Source reference simulations illustrate that per-step rounding differs; they do not define a bank contract. Numerical algorithms, libraries and performance remain technical work. Round 26 defines computed fractional working results as 30 significant digits, nearest with exact ties away from zero; subsequent operations use that working value. This is separate from final display, explicit rounding and cents. Round 28 makes round/floor/ceil operate on the reference fraction of a percentage: round(12.345%; 2) = 12%, not 12.35%. Round a displayed rate coefficient explicitly by multiplying by 100 before round and applying % afterwards. Monetary-amount rounding is unchanged.
help.finance.precisionRule.location: Financial accuracy and rounding section of application help.

help.finance.conditionsRule.text: Monetary inputs are amounts in one currency. Exchange rates, taxes, fees and rules of a particular bank are not inserted automatically. Include the expenses and conditions you need through explicit expressions, your own functions or a calculation sheet.
help.finance.conditionsRule.meaning: Explains the boundary between built-in financial models and user-supplied conditions.
help.finance.conditionsRule.context: Accepted in rounds 21 and 22. Monetary inputs are dimensionless numerical amounts in the same currency; physical quantities are rejected in these positions. No automatic exchange rates, tax, fees or bank contract rules are implied. This does not restrict explicit user calculations or physical-unit conversions elsewhere. Calendar support requested after round 23 is a separate language feature and does not automatically change these financial models to day-count or dated-cash-flow models.

help.copy.percentRule.text: A percentage result copies as a decimal fraction without the percent sign. For example, 30% copies 0.3 with a decimal point or 0,3 with a decimal comma. This applies to result shortcuts, clicks, confirmation and saved history answers. Selected formula text, including 30%, is copied literally. Copying does not change the working percentage value. For a rounded percentage, divide the displayed coefficient by 100 without adding hidden digits or rounding again: 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333. Moving the decimal point can produce more fractional places in the clipboard than the screen shows.
help.copy.percentRule.meaning: Explains the explicitly approved exception to copying the displayed numeric coefficient of a result.
help.copy.percentRule.context: Round 22 corrects percentage-result copy: a displayed 30% copies the decimal fraction 0.3 or 0,3 according to the active number-format locale, without %. This exception applies to editor shortcuts, focused result rows, clicks, confirmation and saved history values in quick mode and sheets. Selected formula text remains literal. It does not change the working percentage semantics or recalculate history. Round 23 accepts copying the displayed percentage coefficient divided exactly by 100, without hidden working digits or another rounding step. Thus 33.3333333333% copies 0.333333333333 (or decimal commas). The ten-fractional-digit screen limit does not truncate the extra places produced by shifting the decimal point in the clipboard value. Grouped identical display entries have the same payload without choosing a latent interpretation. Do not infer number-format locale solely from interface language. No-payback and undefined ROI diagnostics are not ready answers. Round 27 accepts approximately zero as a ready result. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. Exact zero and approximate zero are distinct display entries; identical approximate entries group while retaining every latent value. Multiple visible entries still require choosing. Selected source text remains literal.
help.copy.percentRule.location: Copying help, next to general numeric-result and selected-text rules.

help.finance.argumentsRule.text: Loan functions take (amount; annual_rate; months; timing?), and savings functions take (initial_amount; annual_rate; months; contribution?; timing?). The _period forms take a rate per period and a period count in the same positions. Contribution defaults to 0 and timing to end; start means the beginning of the period. Pass 0 explicitly before timing if there is no contribution. profit and roi take (invested; returned); both payback functions take (invested; net_cash_flow). The ? marks optional arguments in help only. Calls use positional arguments separated by semicolons.
help.finance.argumentsRule.meaning: Explains the approved positional financial signatures and defaults.
help.finance.argumentsRule.context: Accepted in round 22, points 2-4. The question mark is documentation notation, not expression syntax. Localized parameter labels describe positions and do not introduce named arguments. The Latin baseline and one active locale are available together. Round 23 accepts timing as a distinct symbolic value. It can be stored in constants and local variables and passed through or returned by user functions. The protected Latin symbols start/end are always available alongside only the active locale. Equality and inequality between timing values are supported; ordering, arithmetic and numeric 0/1 coercion are rejected. help.finance.boundsRule.text: Loan amounts and whole period counts must be positive. Savings amounts and whole period counts may be zero but cannot be negative. Fractional counts are rejected, not rounded. A rate per period must be greater than -100%; monthly forms check the annual nominal rate after dividing it by 12. Monetary inputs are dimensionless amounts in one currency. Profit allows nonnegative investment and return; ROI requires positive investment. Payback allows zero investment and then returns zero periods.
help.finance.boundsRule.meaning: States accepted financial input boundaries without silently applying banking conventions.
help.finance.boundsRule.context: Accepted in round 22, point 6. Negative rates satisfying a positive growth factor are allowed. This paragraph adds neither a new computation budget nor physical currency-unit grammar.

help.finance.rateConversionRule.text: effective(annual_rate; compounds_per_year) converts an annual nominal rate to an effective annual rate. nominal(annual_rate; compounds_per_year) converts back. The compounding count is required and must be a positive integer. Both results are percentages. For example, effective(12%; 12) is approximately 12.6825%. The nominal rate per compounding period and the effective annual rate must each be greater than -100% for their respective conversion. These functions do not change the rate convention of a monthly calculation.
help.finance.rateConversionRule.meaning: Explains the two explicit annual rate conversions and their mathematically defined domains.
help.finance.rateConversionRule.context: Accepted in round 22, point 5. For m > 0 integer, effective(j; m) = (1+j/m)^m - 1 with j/m > -1; nominal(e; m) = m*((1+e)^(1/m)-1) with e > -1. Domains follow the positive period-growth factor and real-valued model. Percentage copy follows help.copy.percentRule. No numeric algorithm or library has been implemented.

help.percent.displayRule.text: A percentage value is displayed with %: entering 10% shows 10%, and ROI of 30% shows 30%. Its numerical meaning is still the decimal fraction, and 200 + 10% is still 220. Entering the ordinary fraction 0.1 does not automatically make it a percentage. Percentage results copy as decimal fractions. Multiplication and division with numbers or percentages produce an ordinary number: 200 * 10% = 10% * 200 = 20 and 10% * 2 = 0.2. Therefore 200 + 10% * 2 gives 200.2; write 200 + (10 * 2)% to get 240. Sums and differences of rates retain their percent sign. A percentage on the left of an ordinary number uses its fraction: 10% + 200 = 200.1 and 10% - 200 = -199.9. A percentage on the right still gives the relative change: 200 + 10% = 220.
help.percent.displayRule.meaning: Explains the uniform display of percentage-valued expressions without changing their arithmetic.
help.percent.displayRule.context: Rounds 23, 26 and 27. Direct percentage display and scalar/percentage multiplication and division follow their accepted special rules. Percentage on the left of addition/subtraction with an ordinary number uses its numeric fraction and returns an ordinary number. Type-specific handlers retain operand order. The user replaces the prior general function proposal by type-preserving inherited numeric behavior; abs preserves the input type. Round 28 accepts reference-number round/floor/ceil with percentage preservation, ordinary-number percentage power/root results and the documented logarithmic/trigonometric rules. Copying a rate uses the shown coefficient /100; approximately-zero rate copy is 0.

help.evaluation.alternativesRule.text: If one interpretation of an ambiguous formula fails numerically while another succeeds, show the valid answers. For example, a division-by-zero or invalid-function-argument interpretation does not hide a valid result from another interpretation. If no valid answer remains, show a brief error. Incomplete input remains incomplete, and an unselected conditional branch is not evaluated.
help.evaluation.alternativesRule.meaning: Explains filtering numerical failures from alternative interpretations without suppressing all valid answers.
help.evaluation.alternativesRule.context: Accepted in round 23, point 3. Extends the previously accepted final-unit filtering to branch-local evaluation/domain failures. It does not suppress whole-expression syntax errors or unknown names; see help.evaluation.validationRule. Preserve established branch order, display grouping and all remaining answers, including horizontally offscreen entries.

help.evaluation.bindingRule.text: Repeated uses of one named value keep the same interpretation within a calculation. If a = 1m, then a / a is 1 whether a means a metre or a minute; it does not mix the two meanings. Passing that value as a function argument preserves the connection. Separate unit occurrences written directly in a formula remain independent. A later independent calculation can resolve the stored formula using its new context.
help.evaluation.bindingRule.meaning: Explains correlated interpretations of a shared named value rather than independent choices at each use.
help.evaluation.bindingRule.context: Accepted in round 23, point 4. Applies across one calculation or reactive sheet recalculation and through value parameters. It does not permanently freeze a global definition to one selected unit or collapse hidden alternatives just because their formatted results coincide.

help.evaluation.validationRule.text: Syntax and name references are checked throughout the expression, but only the selected conditional branch is evaluated numerically. if(2 > 1; 4; 1/0) returns 4. if(2 > 1; 4; unknown_name) reports the unknown name even though that branch would not be selected. Incomplete input has no ready result.
help.evaluation.validationRule.meaning: Distinguishes whole-expression validation from lazy numerical evaluation.
help.evaluation.validationRule.context: Accepted in round 23, point 6, consistent with saved-definition reference validation. This rule does not by itself require evaluating unit constraints or numerical operations in unused branches. Branch-local numerical failures are described separately in help.evaluation.alternativesRule.

help.calendar.dateInputRule.text: Enter dates as YYYY-MM-DD in any interface language; Russian also accepts DD.MM.YYYY. Use two digits for month and day and four for year. help.calendar.arithmeticRule.text: Add or subtract durations from dates and date-times, and compare or subtract calendar values. 2026-10-09 + 4w3d gives 2026-11-09. Adding whole days to a date keeps a date; a fractional day starts from 00:00 and produces a date-time. A difference between dates is a number of days. Times without dates use the same reference day: 01:00 - 23:00 is -22h. A time crossing midnight retains its day carry: 23:30 + 2h gives 01:30 (+1d).
help.calendar.arithmeticRule.meaning: Explains basic date/duration arithmetic and explicit clock-day carry.
help.calendar.arithmeticRule.context: Rounds 24–25. Date/time multiplication and division are unsupported; duration and calendar-period scalar arithmetic remain distinct. Preserve signed clock-day carry. Date-time differences use fixed offsets without seasonal rules. Date plus clock combines them; date vs date-time comparison/subtraction uses date at 00:00 and the shared system offset. Bare clock vs dated value needs a date.

help.calendar.monthsRule.text: Calendar months and years are separate from fixed-duration units. If the target month lacks the original day, use its last day: 31 January 2026 plus one month is 28 February 2026, and 29 February 2024 plus one year is 28 February 2025. Explicit additions run in order: adding one month twice from 31 January gives 28 March, while adding two months at once gives 31 March. A month cannot become a fixed number of days without a starting date. Write months as mon and years as y; Russian also accepts мес and год. For example, 2026-01-31 + 1mon + 1mon gives 2026-03-28, while 2026-01-31 + 2mon gives 2026-03-31.
help.calendar.monthsRule.meaning: Explains accepted calendar-month/year arithmetic and non-equivalence of sequential additions.
help.calendar.monthsRule.context: Rounds 24–25. Calendar names mon/мес and y/год are approved, with Latin baseline plus the active locale. Aggregate calendar months within one compound period before one clamped shift, then apply the fixed part. Explicit addition operators remain sequential. Fractional months are permitted in intermediate periods but must total an integer at date application. m/м, г and financial period counts are unchanged. Round 31 explicitly replaces the prior Latin month spelling with mon while retaining Russian мес and the stable calendar.unit.month identity; the previous spelling is not kept as an alias.
help.calendar.monthsRule.location: Calendar expressions section of help; completion and diagnostic placement retain their shared interaction rules.

help.calendar.offsetRule.text: UTC and fixed numeric offsets are supported for date-times. If no offset is supplied, use the current system offset shared by the calculation, not a historical or future offset chosen from the entered date. A date without time has no offset. Days are always 24 hours and weeks are seven days; seasonal clock changes are ignored. Append Z or ±HH:mm to a time, with or without a space. Convert with to UTC, ::UTC, or a target such as UTC+01:00. For example, 2026-10-09 14:30+03:00 to UTC gives 2026-10-09 11:30Z. Offset hours are 00–23 and minutes 00–59. Both signed zero offsets display Z. Explicit offsets stay visible; an implicit system offset is not added to the shown answer. The same notation works for a time without a date and keeps its day carry.
help.calendar.offsetRule.meaning: Explains fixed-offset calculation context without regional transition tables.
help.calendar.offsetRule.context: Rounds 24–25 and the explicit instruction to ignore seasonal transitions. Z and UTC stay uppercase in all locales. Suffixes ±HH:mm and targets UTC±HH:mm use hours 00–23 and minutes 00–59; ±00:00 normalizes to Z. Preserve visibility of explicit offsets through calculations/names. Implicit system offsets do not gain a visible suffix. Clock-time conversions preserve signed day carry. No region names or transition tables are introduced.
help.calendar.offsetRule.location: Calendar expressions section of help; completion and diagnostic placement retain their shared interaction rules.

help.calendar.copyRule.text: Calendar answers display dates as YYYY-MM-DD in every language and times in 24-hour form, joining date and time with a space. Keep nonzero seconds and fractional parts; do not add unnecessary zeros. Copy the entire shown answer, including its date, time, day carry and any shown fixed offset. Do not turn it into a numeric timestamp. Selected formula text is copied literally; saved historical answers are not recalculated. Computed time is rounded only for display to the nearest millisecond, with exact ties toward the later time and a point before fractional seconds. A calendar period is copied with all its displayed components and units; fixed durations keep their ordinary numeric-only copy rule.
help.calendar.copyRule.meaning: Explains complete calendar-result copying as distinct from copying a numeric coefficient.
help.calendar.copyRule.context: Rounds 24–25. Applies to current results, clicks, focused rows, quick confirmation, sheets and immutable history under existing readiness/focus rules. Calendar time uses ISO date, 24-hour time, explicit offset/carry and final millisecond rounding; no timestamp conversion. Round 25 copies the complete displayed calendar period with units and both calendar/fixed parts. When the calendar-month component normalizes to zero, it is an ordinary fixed duration and retains numeric-coefficient-only copy. This does not change physical-quantity copy or the percentage fraction exception.
help.calendar.copyRule.location: Calendar expressions section of help; completion and diagnostic placement retain their shared interaction rules.

help.precedence.calendarLiteralsRule.text: A complete 2026-10-09 is one date value. Write 2026 - 10 - 09 to subtract numbers. Russian also accepts 09.10.2026 as a date. A nonexistent complete date is an error, and an incomplete date has no ready result. Time such as 14:30 and date-time such as 2026-10-09 14:30 are also whole values. These token rules do not change the priority of ::, to or arithmetic operators. An offset suffix belongs to the value: 2026-10-09 14:30+03:00. UTC+01:00 is one conversion target. A carried clock such as 01:30Z (+1d) is one value, not multiplication by parentheses. Adjacent calendar components such as 1mon1d also form one period; its months are applied once, then its fixed duration. Separate + operators still apply sequentially.
help.precedence.calendarLiteralsRule.meaning: Explains how whole calendar literals coexist with unchanged operator precedence.
help.precedence.calendarLiteralsRule.context: Rounds 24–25. Whole date/time values include accepted fixed-offset suffixes and explicit carried-clock notation. Parser recovery from incomplete input remains technical grammar work.

help.calendar.periodRule.text: Combine calendar and fixed units in one period: 1y2mon3d. Its years and months are combined and applied once, then its fixed duration. Repeating or reordering components inside the same period does not change it. 2026-01-30 + 1mon1d gives 2026-03-01. Store periods by name, add or subtract compatible components, and multiply or divide the whole period by a number. Fractional months may be intermediate values, but the total must be a whole number when applied to a date: 0.5y is 6mon; 0.5mon is not guessed to mean 15d.
help.calendar.periodRule.meaning: Explains normalization, application order and scalar arithmetic of compound calendar periods.

A clock time alone needs a supplied date before comparison with a dated value.

help.calendar.precisionRule.text: Calculated time keeps finer working fractions and rounds only its final display to the nearest millisecond. Exact ties choose the later time; carry propagates through midnight and the date. Thus 00:00 + 0.4ms + 0.4ms displays 00:00:00.001. A duration alone, 0.4ms + 0.4ms, still gives 0.8ms. Display and copy use a point and at most three fractional-second digits in every language. No 24:00 or date outside years 0001–9999 is displayed. This does not change the numeric round function.

help.numeric.workingPrecisionRule.text: Enter at most 30 significant digits. Computed fractional results are rounded to 30 significant digits, with exact ties away from zero; later operations use that working value. Decimal operations that fit the precision stay exact, such as 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3. The ten fractional places on screen do not round the working value. Integers outside the 30-decimal-digit magnitude limit are errors, not rounded values.

help.numeric.smallValueRule.text: If ten fractional places would turn a nonzero answer into zero, extend its ordinary decimal form to three significant digits, but no more than 30 fractional places. Do not add unnecessary zeros or switch to scientific notation. For example, 0.000000000012345 displays 0.0000000000123. If even this limit rounds it to zero, show ≈ 0. The working value remains nonzero, so later calculations can still use it. Fractional digits after the second remain dimmed. An answer shown as ≈ 0 is ready to copy and copies 0; any unit or percent sign stays only in its display. Its working value remains nonzero.
help.numeric.smallValueRule.meaning: Explains the approved bounded small-number display and approximate-zero correction.
help.numeric.smallValueRule.context: Rounds 26–27. Extend small nonzero coefficients to three significant digits within 30 fractional places. Copy 0 without the approximation marker, unit or percent sign. Keep the unit/percentage suffix in the displayed answer. Ordinary quick confirmation saves the true nonzero typed working value and displayed approximation, and clears or hides only after success. Sheets retain sheet-copy behavior. help.calendar.periodComparisonRule.text: Calendar periods are equal when their normalized month totals and fixed-duration parts are equal: 1y == 12mon is true, 1mon == 30d is false, and (1mon + 3d) == (1mon + 72h) is true. Order pure months or years by their month totals and fixed durations by their lengths. Ordering a mixed period, or a calendar period against a fixed duration, needs a starting date. Apply both to that date, then compare the results; do not assume a month is 30 days.
help.calendar.periodComparisonRule.meaning: Explains component equality and reference-date requirements for calendar-period ordering.
help.calendar.periodComparisonRule.context: Round 26, point 4. Equality and inequality compare normalized components without a reference date. Ordering means <, >, <= or >=. Pure calendar or pure fixed values can be ordered within their own family. The existing calendar.dateRequired diagnostic covers missing reference dates. Date/date-time comparisons are unchanged.

help.numeric.approximateZeroActionsRule.text: An approximately-zero answer is ready: clicking it or using the result-copy shortcut copies 0. Keep its normal suffix on screen, such as ≈ 0 m or ≈ 0%. help.numeric.typePreservingAbsRule.text: abs preserves the kind of value: abs(-1cm) gives a length equal to 1cm and abs(-50%) gives 50%. General numeric operations transform the reference number while retaining the type. The final display may automatically choose a suitable unit scale. Specific operations define their own result-type or dimensional rules.
help.numeric.typePreservingAbsRule.meaning: Explains the user-approved preservation of typed quantities by abs and inherited numeric operations.
help.numeric.typePreservingAbsRule.context: Rounds 27–28. Numeric types inherit operations with type-preserving results by default; applicable percentage handlers take precedence while preserving operand order. The special operation rules are now accepted in round 28. The user also adds automatic result scaling: reference value and type are retained, but input display scale is not fixed. floor(1234mm) displays 1m. Explicit target-unit choice remains authoritative. help.numeric.referenceRoundingRule.text: round, floor and ceil operate on a value’s reference number and preserve its type and scale context. round(12.345%; 2) rounds 0.12345 to 0.12 and displays 12%. floor(1234mm) has a reference result of 1 metre and displays 1000mm, preserving the sole mm scale. To round the written rate coefficient instead, use round(12.345% * 100; 2)%, which gives 12.35%.
help.numeric.referenceRoundingRule.meaning: Explains reference-number rounding separately from the unit used for display.
help.numeric.referenceRoundingRule.context: Round 30 accepts choosing among expression scales by fewest fractional decimal places at working precision before screen rounding, ignoring insignificant trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit scale. Preserve a sole scale, including after functions: floor(1234mm) displays 1000mm; 90s remains 90s. Apply across ordinary measurements, information, fixed duration and derived numerators. Inherit scale context through names/functions; min/max keep selected-value context. Full ladders apply only without scale context. Preserve working values, types, explicit targets and saved historical displays; see language/unit-display.json.

help.numeric.typedRootsRule.text: Powers and roots have specific type rules: a squared length is an area, and sqrt(4m²) gives a length of 2m. A standalone sqrt(4m) has no supported result unit. Percentage powers and roots produce ordinary numbers: (50%)^2 = 0.25 and sqrt(25%) = 0.5. The existing rules for simplifying intermediate units and validating final units still apply.

A percentage on the left does not become a measurement automatically: 10% + 100cm is invalid. Final display may select another scale for the same measured value.

help.numeric.functionTypeRules.text: min and max compare compatible reference values and return the selected value with its type; equal values select the first argument. For example, min(50%; 0.6) gives 50%. Logarithms and trigonometry accept ordinary numbers and percentage fractions, plus the already supported angles for trigonometry. Length, area, mass and duration are not accepted just because they have a reference number. ln(100%) = 0, while sin(1cm) is invalid. Results are ordinary numbers except the already defined angular inverse-trigonometric results.
help.numeric.functionTypeRules.meaning: Explains accepted selection semantics and mathematical function type restrictions.
help.numeric.functionTypeRules.context: Accepted round 28; see language/numbers.json and language/typed-values.md. Typed computation preserves the working value and its type. Copy uses the displayed coefficient under the existing rule. Round 30 accepts choosing among expression scales by fewest fractional decimal places at working precision before screen rounding, ignoring insignificant trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit scale. Preserve a sole scale, including after functions: floor(1234mm) displays 1000mm; 90s remains 90s. Apply across ordinary measurements, information, fixed duration and derived numerators. Inherit scale context through names/functions; min/max keep selected-value context. Full ladders apply only without scale context. Preserve working values, types, explicit targets and saved historical displays; see language/unit-display.json.
help.numeric.functionTypeRules.location: Numeric expressions section of application help.

help.units.automaticScaleRule.text: An explicit conversion target chooses the result unit. Otherwise, keep a single scale used in the expression. With several scales, choose the coefficient with the fewest fractional decimal places before screen rounding, ignoring trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit. 1m + 100mm gives 1100mm; 1m + 1000mm gives 2m; 1km + 1mm gives 1 000 001mm. This also applies to functions, information, fixed durations and derived-unit numerators: floor(1234mm) gives 1000mm and 90s remains 90s. Names and functions carry scale context; min and max use the selected value. Full automatic scale ladders are used only without inherited scale context. Ordinary measurement copy uses the shown numeric coefficient without its unit.
help.units.automaticScaleRule.meaning: Explains the accepted result-scale ranking, context inheritance and fallback boundary.
help.units.automaticScaleRule.context: Round 30 accepts choosing among expression scales by fewest fractional decimal places at working precision before screen rounding, ignoring insignificant trailing zeros; ties choose the larger unit scale. Preserve a sole scale, including after functions: floor(1234mm) displays 1000mm; 90s remains 90s. Apply across ordinary measurements, information, fixed duration and derived numerators. Inherit scale context through names/functions; min/max keep selected-value context. Full ladders apply only without scale context. Preserve working values, types, explicit targets and saved historical displays; see language/unit-display.json. Latin examples illustrate values; standard locale/grouping rules still apply. Do not change a latent unit interpretation to improve its displayed coefficient.

help.precedence.unitTargetsRule.text: A conversion target is a unit or a supported ratio of units: 36km/h to m/s gives 10m/s. Write square and cubic target units as cm2/cm² and cm3/cm³; the suffix is automatically shown as a superscript. cm^2 and cm^3 are not alternative target-unit spellings; use cm² and cm³. To continue arithmetic after to, write (36km/h to m/s) * 2. With the tighter operator, write (36km/h)::m/s * 2 for the same scope. A target contains no numerical factors or arithmetic sum. The next to or :: starts another conversion step. Existing precedence, supported dimensions, numeral-system targets and UTC targets remain unchanged.
help.precedence.unitTargetsRule.meaning: Defines the boundary and accepted notation of a unit-conversion target.
help.precedence.unitTargetsRule.context: Accepted round 30, item 3; see language/unit-input.json. Reuse existing superscript formatting and explicit-target spelling. Do not extend supported final dimensions or interpret a caret as unit-suffix shorthand.

help.completion.unitContextRule.text: Unit suggestions continue the letters you have typed and respect the operation and constraints from surrounding parentheses. After m, square and cubic metre completions appear as m² and m³ when those units fit. In 1cm + 2m…, time, area and volume do not fit the length being added. The same length constraint applies inside 1cm + (2m… * 3). A time divisor may still fit a length calculation. If context is incomplete, keep all prefix continuations that cannot yet be ruled out. After to or ::, offer targets compatible with at least one valid interpretation: after 1m to, cm and s are possible. Selecting a target adds its constraint. Insert the visible spelling without a hidden type choice, and do not duplicate identical inserted spellings.
help.completion.unitContextRule.meaning: Explains prefix continuations filtered by local and outer type constraints, conservative incomplete-context behavior and compatible conversion targets.
help.completion.unitContextRule.context: Accepted rounds 30–31; see language/unit-input.json. The seven-row inline layout, prefix dimming, descriptions, Tab and arrow handling remain unchanged. Calendar month is mon/мес under the separate symbol catalog. General sorting and editing in the middle of a word remain interface decisions.
